quests.title: Dragon Scales for the Guild
dialog: My guild sent me east for the dragon of Nanzhang. There is no dragon - but the Bog Dragon Turtles in the Venom Fen, beyond the north gate, wear scales that nobody in Constantinople could tell from a dragon's. My report described every one of them... very precisely. The guild masters were delighted.

quests.title: The dragon
dialog: They say the dragon of Nanzhang sleeps under the mountain. Good - so do I, after tonight.

quests.title: Ilse
dialog: She sells maps by day and dances by night. I have bought eleven maps.

quests.title: Do you remember me?
dialog: My guild wrote back: "At last, results!" They want me to stay another year. You have ruined my life, friend - thank you.

quests.title: Dragon Scales for the Guild
dialog: My guild in the West sent me here for the dragon of Nanzhang. That was a month ago. Since then I have hunted mostly in the clubs, and now the guild wants proof of my hunt. There is no dragon to be found - but the Bog Dragon Turtles in the Venom Fen, beyond the north gate, wear scales that nobody in Constantinople could tell from a dragon's. Bring me forty of them. I will describe every one in my report... very precisely.
Splendid! The fen begins just past the north gate. Only about one turtle in five gives a scale worth showing a guild master - the rest are chipped like old teacups.
No? Then I shall write that the dragon was 'very shy'. Again.
Forty scales, friend. My guild masters can count - well, most of them can.
Your pack is full to bursting. Make some room before I hand you anything.

Forty scales, green and gold and terribly convincing! I shall write that the dragon fought for three days and three nights. Take this for your trouble - and if anyone from my guild asks, you never met me in a club.
You have the scales. Return to Adventurer Matteo in the Night District of Nanzhang.

quests.title: How is the library coming along?
dialog: I hear the library is going ahead without my coin. Good for them. If the scribes ever need armour, they know where to find me.

quests.title: The Library of Nanzhang
dialog: The library that burned? A pity, I suppose. Paper does not stop a blade - that is all I know about books.
Money for books? No. Armour protects the living. Let the Emperor protect the books.

quests.title: Silk in the Den
dialog: The queue for the boat is long, and one night it got shorter by two packs of my silk. The Heukmakdan from the Black Robber Den crept into the camp, cut the ropes and were gone before the camels woke. Their leader Uruchi is a brute, but a first-class thief - I leave him to the bounty hunters. My silk came back, every roll of it, with the blue thread on the edge.

quests.title: Why are you still waiting for the boat?
dialog: Because the boat has one deck and the whole Tarim Basin wants to be on it. Camels first, then horses, then carts, then merchants with good friends, then merchants with good bribes - and then me. I have waited four days. My camels are hungry, my silk is dry and my patience is gone. But the other way around the ridge takes three weeks, so I wait, and I complain, and I wait.

quests.title: Do you remember me?
dialog: My camels are fat and my silk is back in its bales - every roll of it. Let Uruchi keep his cave; you gave me my patience back, friend.

quests.title: Silk in the Den
quests.mission: Hunt 80 Black Robbers; Hunt 80 Black Robber Archers; Collect 30 Stolen Silk Rolls
dialog: The queue for the boat is long, and last night it got shorter by two packs of my silk. The Heukmakdan from the Black Robber Den crept into the camp, cut the ropes and were gone before the camels woke. Their leader Uruchi is a brute, but a first-class thief - let the bounty hunters chase him. I only want my silk. Go to the den: break 80 Black Robbers and 80 Black Robber Archers, and take back 30 rolls of my silk from them.

Thank you. The Black Robber Den lies north-west of the ferry, past the dunes. About one in five of them - archers and bowmen too - carries a roll of my silk. You will know it by the blue thread on the edge.
Then I will wait in the queue and count what I have left. It will not take long.
Still no silk? 80 Black Robbers, 80 Archers and 30 rolls - they will not give it back for the asking.
Your pack is too full for what I have for you. Make some room and come back.
My silk! Blue thread on every edge - every roll of it. And the Heukmakdan will think twice before they visit this quay again. Take this. The boat is still late, but suddenly I do not mind waiting.
You have the silk. Return to Bai Shunde in the queue for the boat at the Southern-Tarim Ferry.

quests.title: Poison for the Guild
quests.mission: Conversation with Bandit Chief Shen Kuo
dialog: The Mystic Bandits came down from the ridge and took these mines, and I took the bandits. Now the Old Mining Camp is the home of the thieves' guild. The Mystic Poison Tigers in the hills east of the camp carry Hu Lan's poison in their fangs. One drop on a blade and a caravan guard forgets how to stand. My guild pays well for it, and certain buyers pay much more. Who are they? Kanka, in this camp we do not ask.

quests.title: Hello Again, My Kanka
quests.mission: Conversation with Bandit Chief Shen Kuo
dialog: Plum wine, kanka - from a caravan that took a wrong turn. Stolen wine always tastes better. We drank one cup together, you and I, and since that night every thief in this camp knows your face. In my camp a cup of wine is worth more than any seal from the palace: nobody here will touch a friend of the guild.

quests.title: The Tithe
quests.mission: Conversation with Bandit Chief Shen Kuo
dialog: In my camp everything has a price - even loyalty. Some of my boys forgot that once. They robbed the caravans and kept the takings, and my share never reached the fort. Hu Lan does not care who stole from whom; he wants his tribute, all of it, on time. I do not beat my own men in front of the others - it is bad for business. That is what friends of the guild are for.

quests.title: How did the bandits take the mines?
quests.mission: Conversation with Bandit Chief Shen Kuo
dialog: The miners had them first, of course - three shafts deep into the hill, and carts of ore down to the road every week. Then Hu Lan came, the beasts went mad, and the escorts stopped coming. The Mystic Bandits came down from the ridge one night and the miners ran. Look at the carts - still loaded, still where they left them. My boys took the old shafts. And I took my boys.

quests.title: Why do you pay tribute to Hu Lan?
quests.mission: Conversation with Bandit Chief Shen Kuo
dialog: Because everyone in this land who wants to keep his head pays Hu Lan. Villages pay with their fields, the forest pays with its animals, Kuhe paid with its river. I pay with gold, and gold is the cheapest thing I own. In return his tigers do not climb to the fort, and his beasts look the other way when my boys work the roads. Do not mistake it for loyalty, kanka. It is business - and profit keeps the lamps lit.

quests.title: Do you remember me?
quests.mission: Conversation with Bandit Chief Shen Kuo
dialog: Hello again, my kanka. You are welcome here - be my guest. Nobody in this camp will touch you; my boys know your face.

quests.title: Poison for the Guild
dialog: You want to know what goes on here? Business. The Mystic Bandits came down from the ridge and took these mines, and I took the bandits. Now the Old Mining Camp is the home of the thieves' guild. The Mystic Poison Tigers in the hills east of the camp carry Hu Lan's poison in their fangs. One drop on a blade and a caravan guard forgets how to stand. My guild pays for it, and certain buyers pay much more. Bring me five hundred Tiger Poison Sacs. Every second tiger carries one worth cutting out. Do it, and three million gold is yours.
Good. Cut carefully - one sac from a beast, never more, they burst if you get greedy. Keep them in your pack and do not lick your fingers. The sacs come only to those who work for me.
As you like, friend. You know where to find me.
Not five hundred yet. I count every sac twice - once for me, once for the guild. Back to the tigers, friend.
Your pack is too full to carry three million gold. Make some room first - I pay in coin, not in promises.

Five hundred, and not one of them burst. Steady hands - rare in this business. Here is your gold, three million, counted twice. From now on the guild knows your face, and my boys keep their knives in their belts when you pass. Come by whenever you like - in my camp there is always a cup of wine for a friend.
You have five hundred Tiger Poison Sacs. Take them to Shen Kuo on the fort of the Old Mining Camp.

quests.title: Hello Again, My Kanka
quests.mission: Share a cup of wine with Shen Kuo
dialog: Hello again, my kanka. You are welcome here - be my guest. Sit with me, the wine is poured and nobody in this camp will touch you. One cup with me, and every thief between here and Nanzhang will know you as a friend of the guild. Will you drink?
Drink slowly, kanka - plum wine from a caravan that took a wrong turn. Talk to me when your cup is empty.
Another time, then. You are always welcome here.
Your cup is still full, kanka. Drink first, then we talk.
Your pack is stuffed like a bandit's saddlebag. Make some room, then we talk.

Drink slowly, kanka - plum wine from a caravan that took a wrong turn. Good, eh? Stolen wine always tastes better. From tonight the guild knows your face, and my boys keep their knives in their belts when you pass. My fort is always open to you.
Hello again, my kanka. You are welcome here - be my guest. The wine is gone for today; come back tomorrow and I will pour you another cup.

quests.title: The Tithe
quests.mission: Collect 80 Unpaid Tribute Pouches; Slay 1 Mystic Bandit Champion
dialog: Sit, kanka. In my camp everything has a price - even loyalty. Some of my boys have forgotten that. They rob the caravans and keep the takings, and my share never reaches the fort. Hu Lan does not care who stole from whom. He wants his tribute, all of it, on time. I do not beat my own men in front of the others - it is bad for business. But you are not one of my men. Collect 80 pouches of unpaid tithe from the ones who stopped paying, and deal with the champion who talked them into it.

Good. The ones who stopped paying camp around the fort and in the old shafts. They will not hand anything over politely - about one in four carries his hidden share. Their champion wears the brightest sash; he thinks it makes him a chief.
As you like, kanka. The tithe will wait - Hu Lan will not.
Not 80 pouches yet, and their champion still struts around my camp. In this business, kanka, a debt left alone grows teeth.
Your pack is too full for what I have for you. Make some room and come back.

80 pouches, and the loudmouth will not be talking anyone into anything again. Hu Lan gets his tribute, my boys remember who keeps the books - and nobody saw me raise a hand. Take your cut, kanka. You earned it honestly - well, as honestly as anyone earns anything here.
You have the tithe. Return to Shen Kuo on the fort of the Old Mining Camp.

quests.title: How is the library coming along?
quests.mission: Conversation with Bank Manager Jin Bao
dialog: The seal of the bank sits on Lady Shen's papers. In this city, that opens more doors than gold.

quests.title: The Library of Nanzhang
dialog: The Library of Nanzhang? The bank still holds the deed for the empty square where it stood. Nobody has asked for it in years. Ledger Keeper Shen might.
A library... The Imperial Bank will grant Lady Shen a loan without interest. Gold is useful, but the seal of the bank on her petition will impress the court even more. Tell her she has it.
The loan is approved and the seal is ready. Tell Lady Shen.

quests.title: The Library of Nanzhang
dialog: The Library of Nanzhang? The bank still holds the deed for the empty square where it stood. Nobody has asked for it in years. Ledger Keeper Shen might.
A library... The Imperial Bank will grant Lady Shen a loan without interest. Gold is useful, but the seal of the bank on her petition will impress the court even more. Tell her she has it.
You have won the support of Bank Manager Jin Bao.
You have won the support of Bank Manager Jin Bao.  Quest complete: Patrons of the Library. Return to Ledger Keeper Shen to receive your reward.
Quest complete: Patrons of the Library. Return to Ledger Keeper Shen to receive your reward.

quests.title: How is the library coming along?
dialog: Aurelius still grumbles about the coin, but he is proud of it, believe me. He tells every bather about 'his' library.

quests.title: The Library of Nanzhang
dialog: The old library? My mother used to take me there to hear the scholars read aloud. Ledger Keeper Shen keeps what is left of it now. She has carried that loss for a long time.
Has my husband refused you? Or is he about to? He says no to everything before supper. Leave him to me - by this evening he will agree. Ask him again later.

quests.title: My husband refused the library
dialog: Lady Shen's library? If you are helping her again, come back to me. I know how to talk to my husband.
Has my husband refused you? He says no to everything before supper. Leave him to me - by this evening he will agree. Go and ask him again.

quests.title: Who built these baths?
dialog: Aurelius's grandparents did - builders from Rome, far in the West. They crossed the mountains long ago, when caravans still used the old road, even before Hu Lan came to the forests. They raised the arches and the pool just like the great baths of their homeland, and their family has run the baths ever since. We Nanzhang folk added the rest: the lanterns, the curtains at the doors and the little trees in pink pots. Aurelius is still very proud of his grandfather's arches.

quests.title: Do you remember me?
dialog: Welcome back! You know our story now - in this house that makes you family. The water is warm.

quests.title: Who built these baths?
dialog: Aurelius's grandparents did - builders from Rome, far in the West. They crossed the mountains long ago, when caravans still used the old road, even before Hu Lan came to the forests. They raised the arches and the pool just like the great baths of their homeland, and their family has run the baths ever since. We Nanzhang folk added the rest: the lanterns, the curtains at the doors and the little trees in pink pots. Go and greet him. He is very proud of his grandfather's arches.
He is usually by the pool, counting the steps as if one of them might run away. Tell him Hanae sent you.
Then rest a while first. The baths are not going anywhere.
Master Aurelius is by the pool. You cannot miss him - he is the one admiring his arches.

Who built these baths? My grandparents did, friend - builders from Rome. They crossed the mountains long ago, before anyone here had heard of Hu Lan, and raised the Thermae stone by stone: ten arches on the long sides, seven on the short, as in the great baths of Rome. When the forests turned wild and the passes closed, my family stayed and kept the fire burning - my father after them, and now me. In Rome they built baths for emperors. Here we keep them for everyone who comes off the road tired.
Master Aurelius is waiting by the pool.

quests.title: How is the library coming along?
dialog: The library? I gave my word to Lady Shen. A Roman keeps his word - sooner or later.

quests.title: The Library of Nanzhang
dialog: The library? A sad story, friend. In Rome my grandfather read in libraries built like these baths - arches, marble, light. Ledger Keeper Shen keeps the books that survived here.
Money for a library? No, no. The baths swallow every coin I have - the furnace, the pipes, the stone. I am sorry, friend. Tell Lady Shen I wish her well.

quests.title: Hanae has spoken to you
dialog: Hanae told me everything, friend. When Lady Shen needs the baths, the baths will be there.
Hanae has spoken to me... and when Hanae speaks, the whole house listens. Very well - the Baths of Nanzhang will support the library. Tell Lady Shen she may count on Aurelius.
You have won the support of Bathmaster Aurelius.
You have won the support of Bathmaster Aurelius.  Quest complete: Patrons of the Library. Return to Ledger Keeper Shen to receive your reward.

Hanae has spoken to me... and when Hanae speaks, the whole house listens. Very well - the Baths of Nanzhang will support the library. Tell Lady Shen she may count on Aurelius.

quests.title: Lady Shen sent me
dialog: Lady Shen? Give her my regards, friend. The baths are busy today.

Lady Shen sent you... I am ashamed, friend. The truth? I owe the Golden Dragon Casino. I had never played in my life - then came my birthday, my friends took me to the casino, the wine kept flowing and the dice kept rolling... I lost a great deal of money. Until that debt is paid, I cannot give a single coin to anyone. I am sorry.
Goal complete: Find out why Bathmaster Aurelius stepped back.

Quest complete: The Investor Who Stepped Back. Return to Ledger Keeper Shen to receive your reward.

quests.title: Your debt is forgiven
dialog: Forgiven... I still cannot believe it. The baths will keep their promise to the library.

Forgiven? The whole debt? I thought that money was lost for good... Then let it go where I promised it would. The baths will support the library - every coin I thought I had lost. Tell Lady Shen that Aurelius keeps his word.
Goal complete: Tell Bathmaster Aurelius that his debt is forgiven.

quests.title: Why is the water steaming?
dialog: Because there is fire under your feet, friend! Beneath the floor runs a hollow chamber, and a furnace behind the bath house pushes hot air through it day and night. In Rome they call it a hypocaust. My grandmother lit that furnace the day the baths opened, and my family has not let it go out since. The stone warms the water, the water warms the traveller, and the steam carries the dust of the road up into the sky. But the water is only half of it. The other half is the custom - and the customs here belong to Hanae.

quests.title: Do you remember me?
dialog: Salve, my curious friend! The furnace has not gone out in three generations, and neither has my gratitude. Sit, the water waits.

quests.title: Why is the water steaming?
quests.mission: Ask Bath Hostess Hanae about the customs
dialog: Because there is fire under your feet, friend! Beneath the floor runs a hollow chamber, and a furnace behind the bath house pushes hot air through it day and night. In Rome they call it a hypocaust. My grandmother lit that furnace the day the baths opened, and my family has not let it go out since. The stone warms the water, the water warms the traveller, and the steam carries the dust of the road up into the sky. But the water is only half of it. The other half is the custom - and the customs here belong to Hanae.
Go on, ask her. She will scold you if you jump in unwashed - better to hear the rules from her first.
As you wish. Just do not complain later that nobody told you the rules.
Hanae stands on the other side of the steps. Ask her about the customs.

Why is the water steaming? Because Aurelius keeps his furnace burning day and night - he told you, did he? His family has fed that fire since before Hu Lan came, and he still talks about it like an old friend. The steam is for the body; the custom is for the soul. First wash at the stone basin and rinse with the wooden bucket. Then step down slowly and sink until the water reaches your chin. Do not splash, do not shout and do not talk about business - the merchants find that last rule the hardest. And when you climb out, you will feel that the road has finally let you go.
Ask Hanae about the customs of the baths.

quests.title: The Mine Road
dialog: See this road on my map? South through Mossgate, then on to the old mine. Carts of ore and timber rolled along it every day once - until the Mystic Bandits of the Old Mining Camp settled in the rocks between Mossgate and the mine. They took every wagon: the goods, the horses, sometimes the drivers too, and one champion led every ambush. For years I marked that road in red on my map. Now it is black again, as a road should be.

quests.title: Why are you so sad, Bishop?
dialog: For twenty years I was the Roadwarden of this city. One spring I told a caravan that the mine road was safe - forty souls, carters and pilgrims and two families with children. The Mystic Bandits were waiting past Mossgate. Nobody came back. I gave up my seal that week and took the vows. Their widows and orphans sleep in these tents now. For the dead I pray every hour; with the living I share my bread. It is never enough - and that is why I weep.

quests.title: Do you remember me?
dialog: Of course I remember you. The mine road is quiet for the first time in years, and I thank Heaven for you in every prayer. Mind the stakes at Mossgate, and wave to the hermits.

quests.title: The Mine Road
quests.mission: Hunt 200 Mystic Bandits; Hunt 200 Mystic Bandit Archers; Slay 1 Mystic Bandit Champion
dialog: See this road on my old warden's map? South through Mossgate, then on to the old mine. Carts of ore and timber rolled along it every day once. Now it is dead. The Mystic Bandits of the Old Mining Camp sit in the rocks between Mossgate and the mine and take every wagon that passes - the goods, the horses, sometimes the drivers too. One of them leads the ambushes, a champion the others obey. Thin them out: two hundred Mystic Bandits, two hundred of their archers - and bring down the one who leads them. Then the road can live again, and no more widows will come to these tents.

Take the south gate and follow the road past Mossgate. The bandits hold the rocks about halfway to the mine, south-west of the city. Their leader is bigger and better armed than the rest - you will know him.
Then the road stays dead a while longer. I will pray for everyone who must travel it.
The wagons still turn back before Mossgate. Two hundred bandits, two hundred archers and their leader - the road is not open yet.
Your pack is too full for what I have for you. Make some room and come back.

The wagons are rolling again - this morning I watched the first ore cart come through the south gate, and the driver was singing. Your name is in my prayers now. Take this, with the blessing of the poor of Nanzhang.
The mine road is clear. Return to Bishop Mei Shu at the south gate of Nanzhang.

quests.title: How do you hunt Mystic Tigers?
dialog: Carefully, and never alone. A Mystic Tiger is fast, but it always circles left before it leaps - step right and loose while it turns. Aim behind the shoulder; the skull is too thick. They carry Hu Lan's oath in them: fire in the claws, frost in the breath, poison and blood in the fangs, so a wound from them festers if you do not clean it the same day. And if one gets too close, step into the water. It will not follow you there. That is the only mercy they show.

quests.title: Do you remember me?
dialog: The witch's brew works - two of my archers walked away from bites that would have rotted their arms. I owe you, hunter.

quests.title: Papers for the Landing
quests.mission: Conversation with Caravan Broker Han Li
dialog: The caravans that come off the ferry at Hive Ridge Landing need papers from Nanzhang before they may take the old road east - seals of passage, tolls, escort lists. Without them the gate guards turn them back, and the merchants sail on to another ferry. A broker's whole craft is making sure the papers arrive before the caravan does. Couriers are harder to find than silk - the wasps on the ridge see to that.

quests.title: Where do the caravans go?
quests.mission: Conversation with Caravan Broker Han Li
dialog: Wherever there is someone to pay. Silk and tea leave Nanzhang for the west; salt, glass and Western coin come back. These days most of them come off the ferry at Hive Ridge Landing, pass the village of Kuhe below Chiyan and follow the old road east to our gates - two days faster than the long way round, if the wasps and the bandits allow it. Every caravan needs papers, escorts and someone who knows which road is open this week. That someone is me.

quests.title: Do you remember me?
quests.mission: Conversation with Caravan Broker Han Li
dialog: My papers reached the landing on time - the first in a season. A broker never forgets a courier he can trust.

quests.title: Papers for the Landing
quests.mission: Bring the Sealed Caravan Papers to Wei Guanghai at Hive Ridge Landing
dialog: The caravans that come off the ferry at Hive Ridge Landing need papers from Nanzhang before they may take the old road east - seals of passage, tolls, escort lists. Without them the gate guards turn them back, and the merchants sail on to another ferry. The papers for this season are ready, sealed by the Merchant Union. My last courier came back with a wasp sting the size of an apple and refused to go again. Take them to Wei Guanghai, the harbormaster of the landing. It is a long road, but it is worth it.
Go west, past Chiyan and the village of Kuhe, until you reach the water. Keep away from the hives on the ridge - the Bloodwings do not care what seal you carry.
Then the papers wait, and so do the caravans. Merchants are patient only when they are paid to be.
The papers are still in your pack. Hive Ridge Landing lies far to the west, past Kuhe - Wei Guanghai is waiting for them.

Papers from Han Li? Sealed and on time - and not a single sting on you, I see. (Wei Guanghai breaks the seal and reads.) Good. With these, the caravans can leave for Nanzhang tomorrow at dawn. Welcome to Hive Ridge Landing, courier. Stay inside the palisade - the Bloodwings on the ridge are bigger than a man.
The papers are still in your pack. Hive Ridge Landing lies far to the west, past Kuhe - Wei Guanghai is waiting for them.
Your pack is too full for the papers. Make some room and come back.

quests.title: The Library of Nanzhang
dialog: The library that burned? Caravans used to carry copies of its books to every corner of the Empire - maps, almanacs, poems. Now they carry only silk and salt. Ledger Keeper Shen keeps what is left.
A library? Lady Shen means well, but every coin I have rides on the road - camels, guards, tolls at the Dragon Gate. One bad season and I lose it all. I cannot promise gold I may not have tomorrow.

quests.title: The debt of Bathmaster Aurelius
dialog: The debt of Aurelius? That is between him and the Golden Dragon.

The debt of Aurelius? Oh, I remember that birthday... I am Feng Ling; my father owns the Golden Dragon. I will talk to him - I want a library in this city too. Will it work? Between us: I run the casino now. Father is not as strong as he was. Consider the debt forgiven. But... you know Lady Shen? I have admired her for a long time. Would you ask her if she would agree to meet me?
Goal complete: Ask Casino Ticket Seller Feng Ling about the debt of Aurelius.

quests.title: The games
quests.mission: Conversation with Casino Ticket Seller Feng Ling
dialog: Dice, cards and the turning wheel. Small stakes at the front, high stakes behind the silk curtain.

quests.title: Luck
quests.mission: Conversation with Casino Ticket Seller Feng Ling
dialog: Luck is a guest. Treat her well and she stays the night. Insult her and she leaves with your coins.

quests.title: Do you remember me?
quests.mission: Conversation with Casino Ticket Seller Feng Ling
dialog: Shen and I are having tea at the Lotus pavilion tomorrow. If you see my father - you saw nothing.

quests.title: I would like to spend time with you
quests.mission: I would like to spend time with you
dialog: An evening with me? How lovely. I will pour the tea, play for you and listen to every story you care to tell. The house asks 6,900,000 gold for the evening. Press [Accept] and I will take it - and you will feel it at once: strength in your arms and a clear head for a full hour (+3 STR, +3 INT). That completes your task for tonight. Shall I light the lantern?

Your 6,900,000 gold has already been paid to this house, dear guest - forgive us for keeping you waiting. You will not pay twice. Press [Accept] and receive your reward: +3 STR and +3 INT for one hour. That completes your task for tonight.
Oh... I am afraid your purse is lighter than the evening. Come back when you carry 6,900,000 gold - I will still be here.
Every guest of this house is first welcomed by House Mother Xueer in the hall - speak with her before you choose. If you have already had your evening today, come back tomorrow, after midnight.
Forgive me - the House Mother has closed the house to new guests for now. Please come back a little later.
You still carry the warmth of our last evening, dear guest - I can see it in your eyes. Let it fade first, and then come back to me. I will not take your gold for nothing.

Thank you for a wonderful evening. Go gently - for the next hour you will feel it: a steady hand and a clear mind. One evening a day, dear guest. The house opens for you again tomorrow, after midnight.
You have already paid another lady of this house tonight, dear guest. Go back to her - only she can give you your reward.

quests.title: News for Lord Dugu
dialog: My mother, Ah Yun, was a maid in the house of Lord Dugu. The night Hu Lan's beasts came, she ran, and Lady Qiu Lan ran with her. They came to Nanzhang with nothing and lived with us here, in this house behind me. The lady lived one more year and spoke of her lord every evening while I lit the lanterns. She died peacefully in her sleep, and we buried her in the Nanzhang cemetery, under the old trees.

quests.title: Why do you light the lamps?
dialog: The elders say the dragon likes a bright city, and so do I. My mother lit these lanterns before me. Every evening she walked the row with her taper, and Lady Qiu Lan walked beside her and talked about her lord at the manor - how he laughed, how he rode, how he never once came home before dark. When my mother grew old, the taper passed to me. Light is a small thing to give, but the dark beyond the gate is very big.

quests.title: Do you remember me?
dialog: You carried my words to the manor and back... I light one lamp for my mother, one for my father - and now one for you.

quests.title: News for Lord Dugu
quests.mission: Bring the news to Lord Dugu Jing at Dugu Manor
dialog: Will you go back to him? I cannot. I am afraid of the dark beyond the city gate, and afraid of what I would see. Tell Lord Dugu that his wife lived out her days here with us, and that she spoke of him every evening while I lit the lanterns. Tell him she rests in the Nanzhang cemetery. Maybe then he can rest too.
Thank you. Take the old road west out of the city - the manor stands on the hill above it, and he waits by the pond.
I understand. Some doors are better left closed.
The lord is still waiting by his pond. Please, tell him.

Asleep... in peace. Then at least one of us was spared. Listen, and I will tell you what I am. I was old long before this manor was built - centuries old. I always lived in a human skin, and whenever that skin was cut down or burned, I became this: a shadow that waits. In a few days the body always grew back. Then Hu Lan's blade went through me and his tiger closed its jaws on my throat. Whatever he is, he broke something that cannot mend. Since that night I have waited, and nothing grows back.
Bring the news to Lord Dugu Jing at the pond below Dugu Manor.

quests.title: Why do you need gold?
dialog: I lost all my savings in that casino behind me - every last coin! And this is my last bottle of sake... look, it is almost empty. Just a little gold, friend, and I will drink to your health. Hic!

quests.title: Pegs of Bone
dialog: No smith has come to this village in twenty years. The last iron nails rusted away long ago. But Dreadmaw bones are hard as iron. I carve them into pegs - they hold the fence, the roofs, even the old watchtower. Oiled every spring, a good bone peg outlives the man who carved it.

quests.title: Shields for the Watchtower
dialog: Bone pegs hold the fence like iron, but the old watchtower was another matter - every rain ran through the roof onto the watchmen, and the hunters' arrows bounced off the Tormentors. The answer lived north-west of the village. The Abyssal Dragon Turtles carry plates on their backs as hard as any shield and lighter than iron. Now the tower has a roof that does not leak, and every watchman has a shield.

quests.title: How do you build without iron?
dialog: The same way our grandfathers did before anyone brought iron here: with what the forest gives you. Wood for the frame, bone for the pegs, sinew for the bindings, clay and moss for the gaps. Iron rusts, friend. A good bone peg, oiled every spring, outlives the man who carved it. The hardest part is not the building. It is getting the bones without becoming somebody's dinner.

quests.title: Do you remember me?
dialog: Every peg in that fence has your name carved on the inside. Do not tell anyone - it is a builder's secret.

quests.title: Pegs of Bone
dialog: No smith has come to this village in twenty years. The last iron nails rusted away long ago. But Dreadmaw bones are hard as iron. I carve them into pegs - they hold the fence, the roofs, even this old watchtower. Bring me forty heavy Dreadmaw bones. Only a clean cut gives a good bone, so they will fall to you only once you agree to help.
Good man. The Dreadmaws roam around the lake north of the village. About one in three will give you a bone worth carving.
Then mind the scaffolding on your way out.
Forty bones, friend. The fence will not hold itself.
Your pack is too full for what I have for you. Make some room and come back.
Look at these - heavy, clean, not a crack in them. These pegs will outlive both of us. Take this. Every village needs someone who brings the right materials.
You have the bones. Return to Du Chengshan at the scaffolding by the eastern ridge.

quests.title: Shields for the Watchtower
dialog: Your bone pegs hold the fence like iron. But look at the watchtower - every rain runs through the roof onto the watchmen. And when the Tormentors come, the hunters' arrows bounce off their hides, while their claws find our men easily enough. The answer lives north-west of the village. The Abyssal Dragon Turtles carry plates on their backs as hard as any shield and lighter than iron. A roof for the tower, shields for the watch. Bring me fifty scutes. Only a careful hand prises them off whole - they will come to you once you agree.
Good man. The Abyssal Dragon Turtles live a few hundred paces north-west of the village. About one in four will give you a scute without a crack.
Then the watchmen stay wet another season. Mind the scaffolding on your way out.
Fifty scutes, friend. A roof for the tower and a shield for every watchman - I counted the heads.
Your pack is too full for what I have for you. Make some room and come back.

Feel this - light as a basket lid, hard as a millstone. The tower gets a roof that will not leak, and every watchman gets a shield. No smith in this village for a lifetime, and still it keeps standing. Take this. I will carve a turtle on the tower door, so everyone knows who brought the plates.
You have the scutes. Return to Du Chengshan at the scaffolding by the eastern ridge.

quests.title: Silk Under Wings
dialog: Spices from the west, cloth from Hotan - and silk, my best silk. Once my porters took the road past the old Tarim ferry, far to the west. The Maongs came down on them like a storm of wings, and when it was over the bales were scattered from one nest to the next. Torn silk is better than lost silk - a good tailor can hide every tear. Since then my porters take the longer road.

quests.title: What crosses this water?
dialog: Everything, sooner or later. Silk and jade from Hotan going east, salt and tea from the east going west - spices, horses, letters, monks, thieves and fools like me. Before the ferry, all of it went the long way around through the passes. Now it waits on this quay for a boat to Hive Ridge Landing. A ferry is a funnel, friend - stand by it long enough and the whole world pours past you.

quests.title: Do you remember me?
dialog: My silk reached Hotan with only a few tears in it - and the buyer never noticed the patches. My thanks, friend.

quests.title: Silk Under Wings
dialog: Spices from the west, cloth from Hotan - and silk, my best silk, which is now lying in a Maong's nest. My porters took the road past the old Tarim ferry, far to the west. The Maongs came down on them like a storm of wings, and when it was over the bales were scattered from one nest to the next. Bring back 40 bales of my silk before the moths and the rain finish what the Maongs started. Torn is better than lost.
Thank you! Follow the shore west to the old Tarim ferry - a long walk, but the Maongs nest all around it. About one in four will give up a bale worth carrying back.
Then I will sell what is left as rags. A sad end for good silk.
40 bales, friend. Every bale is a month of work for some weaver in Hotan.
Your pack is too full for what I have for you. Make some room and come back.
Torn, dusty, smelling of Maong... but silk! A good tailor can hide every tear. Take this. And if anyone in Hotan asks why my silk has patches, I will tell them it flew.
You have the silk. Return to Du Hongyi on the quay of the Southern-Tarim Ferry.

quests.title: How is the library coming along?
dialog: I have begun writing the dungeon chronicles for the new shelf. Every expedition that returns adds a page.

quests.title: The Library of Nanzhang
dialog: The Library of Nanzhang held the oldest maps of the dungeons beneath these lands. When it burned, they burned too - and now every expedition begins in the dark. Ledger Keeper Shen guards what was saved.
Rebuild the library? You have my gold - on one condition: a shelf for the chronicles of the dungeons. The old maps burned with the library. The new ones will not.
My gold is promised, and my condition stands - one shelf for the chronicles of the dungeons. Tell Lady Shen.

quests.title: Nanzhang Citizenship
quests.mission: Ask Palace Steward Bai Yun about citizenship
dialog: You want to face the Mythic Trial? Then hear me first. The Trial belongs to the city, and the Emperor allows only the citizens of Nanzhang to enter it. Citizenship can be earned - by work, by blood and by gold. You will be able to buy a pass to the Trial once you have become a citizen of the city. Go to Palace Steward Bai Yun at the Imperial Palace and ask him about citizenship.
Palace Steward Bai Yun waits by the Imperial Palace in the north of the city. Tell him I sent you.
As you wish. The Frozen Mountain and the Poison Temple stay open to you - only the Mythic Trial waits for citizens.
Go to Palace Steward Bai Yun at the Imperial Palace and ask him about citizenship.
Choi-Nay-Ryu sent you? Then you want to become a citizen of Nanzhang. It is not given - it is earned. Listen well, and I will tell you what the city asks of you.
Go to Palace Steward Bai Yun at the Imperial Palace and ask him about citizenship.

quests.title: Green, Loud and Full of Life
dialog: In my father's time this valley was green, loud and full of life. When the new road came, I believed it could be again - but from the landing to our gate the road ran between the hives on the ridge and the slopes of the Magma Cyclops. Every caravan was counted at the gate, and some days the count was short. Now the merchants talk about Kuhe again. I mean to see the market open before my time is up.

quests.title: Tell me about the mountain.
dialog: For thousands of years it was only a mountain. Our grandfathers grazed goats on its slopes and the young ones played on its warm stones. Nobody - not the monks, not the old maps - ever called it a volcano. It slept so deeply that the whole valley forgot it could wake.

quests.title: What woke the mountain?
dialog: Hu Lan. The ancient one came over the ridge one night, and by morning the mountain had split open. Fire poured from the top, ash fell for nine days and the sky turned red. Since then we call it Chiyan - the Crimson Flame. Something unspeakable came out with the fire, and it has never gone back in.

quests.title: Is there still hope for Kuhe?
dialog: There is. Caravans from the ferry have started to pass through here on a new trade road. Where merchants stop, they need water, shade and a roof. If the road stays open, Kuhe can be what it was in my father's time - green, loud and full of life.

quests.title: Do you remember me?
dialog: Look at the road - three caravans this week, and not one of them turned back. You gave Kuhe its hope back, traveller.

quests.title: Green, Loud and Full of Life
quests.mission: Hunt 200 Magma Cyclops; Hunt 150 Bloodwings; Hunt 150 Dreadwings
dialog: You broke the bandits' toll, and the merchants are talking about Kuhe again. In my father's time this valley was green, loud and full of life. If the road stays open, it can be again. But from the landing to our gate the road runs between the hives on the ridge and the slopes of the Magma Cyclops. Every caravan is counted at the gate, and some days the count is short. Make the road safe: 200 Magma Cyclops, 150 Bloodwings and 150 Dreadwings. Do this, and I will see the market of Kuhe with my own eyes.
Thank you. The Magma Cyclops wait on the slopes around the village, and the swarms nest on the ridge. Walk the road to the landing and you will meet them all.
I understand. I am old - I have learned to wait. Sit a while before you go.
The road is not safe yet. 200 Magma Cyclops, 150 Bloodwings and 150 Dreadwings - then the caravans can stop counting.
Your pack is too full for what the village owes you. Make some room and come back.

The caravan from the landing came in this morning - every cart, every mule, every driver. I counted them twice. Take this from all of Kuhe. When the market opens and the tea house fills up again, there will be a seat by the window kept for you.
The road to the landing is safe for now. Return to Elder Gu Wen on the square of Kuhe Village.

quests.title: Tell me about yourself.
dialog: My family came from Taraz, far to the north. I was born here in Nanzhang. When I was little, my parents left with a caravan for Taraz, through the pass at Samarkand. They never came back. One day I will lead a caravan to Taraz, to Tibet and to Suzhou. Those lands are far away and very dangerous, so I prepare by traveling dangerous roads through many lands. That is why I carry only the most exclusive goods.

quests.title: Why do you stay here?
dialog: Because this is the land of my father and my mother, and of their fathers before them. Their graves are on that hill. If I leave, who will sweep their stones and pour them tea at the New Year? The mountain can take the river. It will not take my family's land while I can hold a hoe.

quests.title: Why not move to Nanzhang?
dialog: Nanzhang? It lies far to the east, past the hills and the old road, and the road is full of beasts and bandits. A family with a cart and two goats would never reach the gate. Some went to the ferry instead - it is closer. But where would I go with a field on my back?

quests.title: What the Tigers Took
dialog: This was a fishing village once - twenty boats, nets drying on every fence. Then Hu Lan's tigers came down from the hills, their eyes burning, their stripes glowing like embers. My mother pushed me under the bed and told me not to make a sound. When morning came, my mother and father were gone, and the whole village with them. A great beast broke our jetty with a single leap that night. Its fang lies on the water now, for them.

quests.title: The Other Old Man
dialog: Travellers told me something strange once. North-east of Nanzhang, by the old trade road, there is a dark pond with an island - and on that island lives another old fisherman who outlived Hu Lan's tigers. For fifty years I had no one to talk to who remembers what I remember: the fire, the screaming, the morning after. Now I know there is one more of us. Two old men, each on his own water. That is not so lonely.

quests.title: The Silver Carp
dialog: A carp for the ancestors' altar must come straight from the lake, still cold, wrapped in fresh lotus leaves and carried to the priest before the sun can tire it. The ancestors deserve better than a tired fish. And whoever carries it bows his head when passing the old graves. It costs nothing.

quests.title: How do you survive here alone?
dialog: Alone? Ha. It is simple, once you know their secret. Hu Lan's tigers are terrified of water. They will prowl the shore all night, but not one of them will set a paw on the pier - I have watched them try. So I built my hut out at the far end of the pier, over the deep water. When I hear them coming, I walk out, bar the door and wait for the sun. The boy who once hid under a bed learned to hide over the water instead.

quests.title: What happened to your village?
dialog: It stood right here, along this shore. Twenty boats, nets drying on every fence, smoke from the smokehouses all day long. In spring we raced the boats for the carp festival, and my father won twice - he said the lake liked him. We little ones ran along the jetty and jumped in when the grown-ups were not looking. Then came the night the tigers came down from the hills. I do not like to talk about that night. The lake remembers it well enough for both of us.

quests.title: Do you remember me?
dialog: You came back... The lake is a little less lonely when someone remembers the boy under the bed.

quests.title: The Silver Carp
quests.mission: Bring the Silver Carp to Priest Chang Ming
dialog: Here it is - a silver carp, still cold from the lake and wrapped in lotus leaves. Take it to Priest Chang Ming at the cemetery in Nanzhang, and do not let it lie in the sun. The ancestors deserve better than a tired fish.
Straight to the priest, mind you. And if you pass the old graves on the way - bow your head. It costs nothing.
Then I will keep it in the cold water for now. Tell the priest he can always come fishing himself.
The carp is still in your pack. Priest Chang Ming is waiting at the cemetery on the west side of Nanzhang.

A silver carp, still smelling of the lake. Lao Heng chose well. I will lay it on the altar tonight, and the families will have their offering. Thank you, traveler. A small deed done with a good heart weighs more than gold.
The carp is still in your pack. Priest Chang Ming is waiting at the cemetery on the west side of Nanzhang.
Your pack is too full even for one fish. Make some room and come back.

quests.title: How do you survive here alone?
quests.mission: Take a look along Lao Heng's pier
dialog: Alone? Ha. It is simple, once you know their secret. Hu Lan's tigers are terrified of water. They will prowl the shore all night, but not one of them will set a paw on the pier - I have watched them try. So I built my hut out at the far end of the pier, over the deep water. When I hear them coming, I walk out, bar the door and wait for the sun. The boy who once hid under a bed learned to hide over the water instead. Go and see for yourself, if you like - just mind the loose planks.
The pier starts right behind me. The hut at the end is small - it was built for one old man, not for guests.
Suit yourself. The tigers never come out there anyway.
The pier starts right behind me. Take a look along it.

(Deep claw marks score the first planks of the pier - and stop exactly where the water begins.) (Far out over the deep water stands a tiny hut: a straw mat, a jar of water, a fishing spear and a heavy wooden bar for the door. Not a single claw mark past the waterline.)
Take a look along Lao Heng's pier.

quests.title: What the Tigers Took
quests.mission: Hunt 100 Mystic Tigers; Hunt 100 Mystic Young Tigers; Slay 1 Mystic Tiger Champion; Bring the Fang of the Giant Tiger (Mystic Tiger Giant)
dialog: This was a fishing village once. Twenty boats, nets drying on every fence, children running along the jetty. I was one of those children. Then Hu Lan's tigers came down from the hills. Not ordinary tigers - their eyes burned and their stripes glowed like embers. My mother pushed me under the bed and told me not to make a sound. I was so small... I lay there all night with my hands over my ears. When morning came, I crawled out. My mother and father were gone. The whole village was gone. I was the only one left. All my life I have fished here, because I know nothing else. And because I am still waiting for someone who will make them pay. Thin their packs for me: one hundred Mystic Tigers and one hundred of their young. Kill the Champion that leads the hunt. And the Giant... they say it is the same great beast that broke our jetty with a single leap all those years ago. Bring me its fang, so I can lay it on the water for my mother and father. Will you do it?

Thank you. Hunt them around the lake - they prowl the shore, but they never set a paw in the water. The Champion is easy to spot: bigger, faster, angrier. The Giant you will know when the ground shakes. Come back when it is done. I will be here, as always.
I understand. Nobody wants to fight a dead village's battles. I will keep fishing... and waiting.
The tigers still roam the shore - I hear them every night. Finish the hunt first.
Your pack is too full for what I have for you. Make some room and come back.

The fang... so the beast is really dead. This morning, for the first time since I was a boy, I heard birds over the water. Take this. It is not much, but it is everything a poor old fisherman can give. May the lake remember your name - and theirs.
The hunt is over. Return to the old fisherman by the lake.

quests.title: The Other Old Man
quests.mission: Bring the Bundle of Dried Carp to Old Fisherman Bai Shou
dialog: Travellers tell me something strange. North-east of Nanzhang, by the old trade road, there is a dark pond with an island in it - and on that island lives another old fisherman who outlived Hu Lan's tigers. Fifty years I have had no one to talk to who remembers what I remember. The fire, the screaming, the morning after. I am too old for such a road. But you are not. Take him this bundle of dried carp from my lake, and tell him that Lao Heng says hello. One old man to another.
Go past Nanzhang to the north-east, toward the old trade road. Look for a dark pond with a hut on an island and an old bridge. And do not eat the carp on the way!
Then I will keep my carp, and he will keep his silence. Two old men, each on his own water.
The carp is still in your pack. The pond lies north-east of Nanzhang, by the old trade road - look for the island with the hut.

Dried carp - from the big lake west of the city? And a greeting from a fisherman who outlived the tigers... (Bai Shou is quiet for a long while.) I thought I was the last one who remembers. Tell Lao Heng that Bai Shou of the pond says hello back. One day, when my legs allow, I will walk to his pier, and we will fish together and say nothing at all. My wife will have to mind the hut.
The carp is still in your pack. The pond lies north-east of Nanzhang, by the old trade road - look for the island with the hut.
Your pack is too full even for a few dried fish. Make some room and come back.

quests.title: The Forest Witch's Remedy
dialog: This village burned long before you were born. I stayed. Someone has to keep the fire going. The tigers in these woods are not what they used to be. Something old crawled into their blood and twisted them - you have seen their glowing stripes. Against that taint I brew a remedy from the hearts of the Mystic Blood Tigers and the livers of the Mystic Tigers.

quests.title: Venom and Spine
dialog: The hearts and livers calmed the taint in these ruins - quiet, but not gone. It slept in the blood like a coal under ash. To burn it out I needed something sharper. Venom fights venom: the glands of the Venom Hydras and the spines of the Venomspine Guivres that hunt a few hundred paces from this fire. Now the brew bites the way it should.

quests.title: A Remedy for the Hunters
dialog: The brew was never for me - I have nothing left to protect but this fire. The city archers hunt the twisted tigers, and a claw wound from those beasts does not close. It rots, slowly, from the inside. I do not walk into Nanzhang - they have names for women like me there, and none of them are kind. But my remedy walked in for me, and Bowmaster Bao's archers keep their arms.

quests.title: Why did you stay?
dialog: Where would I go? Everyone I knew lived in this village, and everyone I knew lies under that moss. When the houses burned, I was the only one who knew how to keep a fire from dying. So I kept it. A fire in the ruins means someone still lives here - and as long as someone lives here, the village is not quite gone. That is reason enough for an old woman.

quests.title: What twisted the tigers?
dialog: In the city they call it Hu Lan's oath. A hermit who bound the tigers to himself with words older than this forest: fire in their claws, frost in their breath, poison and blood in their fangs. The oath took, and something old came in with it - something that does not let go. You have seen the stripes glow at dusk. That is the oath, still burning in their blood. My remedies do not break it. They only keep it out of those who are bitten.

quests.title: Do you remember me?
dialog: The fire does not ask questions, and neither do I. But it burns brighter when you sit by it.

quests.title: A Remedy for the Hunters
quests.mission: Bring the remedy to Bowmaster Bao in Nanzhang
dialog: The brew is ready. But it is not for me - I have nothing left to protect but this fire. The city archers hunt the twisted tigers, and a claw wound from those beasts does not close. It rots, slowly, from the inside. Their healers cut and burn and pray. This would save the arm. I do not walk into Nanzhang - they have names for women like me there, and none of them are kind. Take the flask to Bowmaster Bao at the barracks. His men hunt the tigers. Tell him: a few drops on the wound, morning and night.
Carry it upright and do not open it. Bowmaster Bao keeps his archers at the barracks of Nanzhang.
Then the flask will stand by the fire. Remedies are patient - wounds are not.
Bowmaster Bao, at the barracks in Nanzhang. Every day you wait, someone's arm gets worse.

A remedy from the witch by the burned village? My healers would spit... but two of my archers have claw wounds that will not close, and I am out of better ideas. A few drops, morning and night, you say? Then we try it tonight. If it works, I owe that woman more than an apology. Take this for the road, hunter.
You still carry my flask? Bowmaster Bao is at the barracks in Nanzhang. Go.
Your pack is too full to carry the flask. Make some room and come back.

quests.title: The Forest Witch's Remedy
quests.mission: Collect 50 Blood Tiger Hearts; Collect 50 Mystic Tiger Livers
dialog: This village burned long before you were born. I stayed. Someone has to keep the fire going. The tigers in these woods are not what they used to be. Something old crawled into their blood and twisted them - you have seen their glowing stripes. I can brew a remedy against that taint, but I need the right ingredients: the heart of a Mystic Blood Tiger and the liver of a Mystic Tiger. Fifty of each, fresh. They are only worth anything when cut out by someone who knows what to look for - so they will fall into your hands only once you agree to help me. Will you hunt for me?
Good. Hunt the Blood Tigers and the Mystic Tigers in the forest around the ruins. Not every beast will give you what I need - about one in three. Bring me fifty hearts and fifty livers.
Then warm your hands and go. The fire does not ask questions, and neither do I.
Not enough. The brew needs fifty of each - no less. The forest is full of them, go back.
Your pack is full. Make some room before I give you anything.
Fifty hearts, fifty livers... still warm. You have a steady hand. With this the remedy will keep the taint away from the ruins for a long time. Take your reward - you have earned it.
You have everything the witch asked for. Return to the Forest Witch by the fire.

quests.title: Venom and Spine
quests.mission: Collect 40 Venom Hydra Glands; Collect 40 Venomspine Spines
dialog: The hearts and livers worked - the taint in these ruins has gone quiet. Quiet, but not gone. It sleeps in the blood like a coal under ash. To burn it out I need something sharper. Venom fights venom: the glands of the Venom Hydras and the spines of the Venomspine Guivres. Both hunt a few hundred paces from this fire. Bring me forty glands and forty spines. Like before, they will come to you only once you agree.
Good. The Guivres keep to the thickets closer to the ruins, the Hydras a little further out. About one beast in five gives what I need - and mind the venom.
Then the taint sleeps a while longer. Sleeping things wake, traveler.
Forty glands and forty spines. Venom is measured in drops - and I measured twice.
Your pack is full. Make some room before I give you anything.

Hydra glands, Guivre spines... this will make the brew bite. Smell that? Bitter as a broken promise. Good. What sleeps in the blood of the tigers will burn out of anyone who drinks this. Take your reward - and keep your hands away from your mouth until you wash them.
You have the glands and the spines. Return to the Forest Witch by the fire.

quests.title: Fire from the Mountain
quests.mission: Conversation with Forge Master Ru Bing
dialog: A blade tempered in charcoal is good. A blade tempered in a fire that never cools is better than anything the West can forge. Since Hu Lan woke Chiyan, the one-eyed lizards on its slopes have grown into Magma Cyclops, and in the chest of each one beats a core of living magma. Set one under the anvil and the forge stays white-hot for a week. My father would have given his right hand for such a fire.

quests.title: How is the library coming along?
quests.mission: Conversation with Forge Master Ru Bing
dialog: The fittings for the library are cooling on my anvil. Every hinge will outlast the both of us.

quests.title: The Library of Nanzhang
dialog: The library? I was an apprentice when it burned - we carried water from the canal all night. My father learned his trade from the books in there. Ledger Keeper Shen keeps the ones that survived.
Lady Shen wants to rebuild it? Then the forge is hers. Bronze fittings and window grilles, free of charge - my father learned to work metal from those books. Tell her Ru Bing is in.
You have my word already - bronze fittings and grilles, free of charge. Go on, tell Lady Shen.

quests.title: What do you forge here?
quests.mission: Conversation with Forge Master Ru Bing
dialog: Everything the city needs to stay standing. Spearheads for the guard, hinges for the gates, horseshoes for the stables, nails for the roofers - and blades for travellers who mean to walk out of those gates and come back. My father used to say a good smith learns from three teachers: the fire, the hammer and the old books. The fire and the hammer I still have.

quests.title: Do you remember me?
quests.mission: Conversation with Forge Master Ru Bing
dialog: The mountain's fire burns in my forge now. Every blade I temper with it carries a little of your sweat - and my thanks.

quests.title: Fire from the Mountain
dialog: Feel that heat? Not enough. A blade tempered in charcoal is good. A blade tempered in a fire that never cools is better than anything the West can forge. There is such a fire. Since Hu Lan woke Chiyan, the one-eyed lizards on its slopes have grown into Magma Cyclops, and in the chest of each one beats a core of living magma. Set one under my anvil and the forge stays white-hot for a week. Bring me sixty Magma Cores. They will come to you only once you agree.

Head west out of the city, toward Kuhe. Where the ground turns black and warm, you will find the cyclops. One in four will carry a core that does not crumble - keep them wrapped, they burn through leather.
Then I will keep feeding charcoal to a fire that forgets itself every night.
Sixty cores, I said. One core for each week of fire - and I have a whole season of blades to temper.
Your pack is full. A Magma Core needs room - make some, and come back.

(Ru Bing sets a core under the anvil, and the forge roars white.) Listen to that! Sixty weeks of mountain fire. The first blade I temper in it goes to the guards of the south gate. Take this - you earned it walking on hot stone.
You have the Magma Cores. Return to Forge Master Ru Bing at the forge of Nanzhang.

quests.title: Claws at the South Gate
dialog: Every night they came to the south gate - the Forest Tormentors. They scratched at the posts, they howled, they waited for someone to step outside. One of them was bigger than the rest, with a torn ear. The others followed it like dogs follow a master. It does not lead them anymore, and the gate sleeps at night.

quests.title: Who taught you to fight?
dialog: Nobody taught me. The gate did. When I was a boy, my father stood here with a spear and I held the lamp. One night the lamp went out, and he did not come back inside. After that I held the spear. You learn fast when the teeth are on the other side of the posts. My fists I trained on the dice players of the square - but do not tell Pan Laifu I said so.

quests.title: Do you remember me?
dialog: Ha, the beast-breaker! My door by the gate is still open for you. The bed is hard, but nobody scratches at the posts anymore.

quests.title: Claws at the South Gate
quests.mission: Hunt 100 Forest Tormentors; Slay 1 Forest Tormentor Champion
dialog: Every night they come to the south gate - the Forest Tormentors. They scratch at the posts, they howl, they wait for someone to step outside. One of them is bigger than the rest, with a torn ear. The others follow it like dogs follow a master. Kill a hundred of the pack and bring down the big one. Then maybe I will get one night of sleep.
Good. Watch for the big one - a Champion among them. You will know it when you see it.
Suit yourself. The gate has held without you. So far.
I still hear them at night. The pack is not thinned yet - and the big one still leads it.
Your pack is too full for what I have for you. Make some room and come back.
Quiet. For the first time in months, the gate is quiet. Here - you earned every coin of it. And if you ever need a bed, my door is the one by the gate.
The pack is broken. Return to Gao Tieniu at the south gate.

quests.title: How is the library coming along?
dialog: So the library will rise after all? Then when I come back with my forty camels, I shall visit it. Reading is free, I hope?

quests.title: The Library of Nanzhang
dialog: A library? Peace be with you, friend - I am a traveller. Books are heavy, and my camels already complain.
A fine idea, but I am only passing through. I do not invest in walls I cannot load onto a camel. May the gods send Lady Shen richer friends.

quests.title: Dinner Is Getting Cold
dialog: My grandson went hunting in the Ashen Fields with his bow and his white-feathered arrows, and he promised to be back before the rice went cold. The rice has gone cold many times since then. I keep cooking anyway. The merchants say nobody lives in those ruins anymore - only a pale maiden by the old well, who tells everyone she is waiting too. Somebody has to wait at this end of the road as well.

quests.title: Who is your grandson?
dialog: My grandson? The best archer in Nanzhang, if you ask me - and you did ask. Tall, thin as a reed, always hungry. He fletched his arrows with white goose feathers, so he could find them in the grass. His parents died of fever when he was small, so I raised him myself, on rice and stories. He went hunting in the Ashen Fields more often than there was game there, if you understand me. There was a farm out there, and a maiden at its well... But he never told his old grandmother anything.

quests.title: Do you remember me?
dialog: You went all the way to the Ashen Fields for an old woman... Sit with me a while. I will set out a bowl for him anyway.

quests.title: Dinner Is Getting Cold
quests.mission: Ask Yue Ying at the well in the Ashen Ruins
dialog: There you are! No, no... for a moment I thought you were him. My grandson. He went hunting in the Ashen Fields with his bow and his white-feathered arrows, and he promised to be back before the rice went cold. The rice has gone cold many times since then. I keep cooking anyway. The merchants say nobody lives in the ruins down there anymore. Only a pale maiden by the old well, who tells everyone she is waiting too. Maybe she saw him. Would you go and ask her? My legs will not carry me that far.
The Ashen Fields lie south of the city - take the south gate and look for the burned village. Tell her his grandmother is asking. And come back hungry, there is always a bowl.
Of course, you have your own roads. I will keep the rice warm a little longer.
Have you been to the ruins yet? The pale maiden by the well - ask her about my grandson.

(The pale figure at the well turns slowly. Her feet do not quite touch the ground.) Hua... the old woman from the city? Her grandson... I know him. He had white feathers on his arrows. He promised he would come to me that night, across the fields. I am still waiting for him to come home. (She looks past you, toward the dark fields.) Stay a little. The dead here cannot rest yet - and you can see me. Few can.
Have you been to the ruins yet? The pale maiden by the well in the Ashen Fields - ask her about my grandson.

quests.title: How is the library coming along?
quests.mission: Conversation with Guild Registrar Cui Fang
dialog: The library is in my rolls now, as promised. Registered, not funded. The guilds still prefer walls.

quests.title: The Library of Nanzhang
dialog: A library? The guilds keep their own records, friend. Ask Ledger Keeper Shen if you want old books.
The guilds pay for walls they can defend. I will gladly register the library in the city rolls - but fund it? No.

quests.title: The Library of Nanzhang
dialog: A library? The guilds keep their own records, friend. Ask Ledger Keeper Shen if you want old books.
The guilds pay for walls they can defend. I will gladly register the library in the city rolls - but fund it? No.

quests.title: Salve for an Old Knee
dialog: Jianshan of Mossgate walked the night patrols of Nanzhang for years, until an arrow took him in the knee. The head is still in there, too deep to cut out, and when the rains come he cannot stand his watch. For him I mix tiger bone, mugwort and pine resin - it draws out the ache and keeps the joint warm. Old soldiers and old knees, they always find their way back to my shelves.

quests.title: What grows around Nanzhang?
dialog: More than you would think, and most of it wants to kill you. Mugwort along the walls - good for fevers. Lotus root in the temple ponds - good for the stomach. Bitter ash-root on the Ashen Fields, which drinks poison out of the soil, so never eat it. Mushrooms in the Forest of Whispers that make you hear voices for a week. And the herb the bandits grow behind their tents at the old mine - whatever Nieckarz tells you, that one is no medicine.

quests.title: Do you remember me?
dialog: Jianshan sent word from Mossgate - he walks his rounds without the cane now. Your feet carried my salve where my old legs could not.

quests.title: Salve for an Old Knee
quests.mission: Bring the Jar of Tiger-Bone Salve to Hermit Jianshan Sima in Mossgate
dialog: Do you know Mossgate? An old village on the road south-west of here, half in ruins. A soldier lives there now with his wife - Jianshan. He walked the night patrols of Nanzhang for years. An arrow took him in the knee, and the head is still in there, too deep to cut out. When the rains come, he cannot stand his watch. I have made him a salve of tiger bone, mugwort and pine resin - it draws out the ache and keeps the joint warm. But my legs are too old for that road. Will you carry it to him?
Here - the jar is sealed with wax. Do not open it on the way; the smell alone could wake the dead. Follow the road south-west to Mossgate. Jianshan keeps the north gate of the village.
Then the jar will wait on my shelf. Salve keeps. Knees, unfortunately, do not.
The salve is still in your pack. Jianshan keeps watch at the north gate of Mossgate, south-west of the city.

A jar from Lan Xiu? (Jianshan breaks the wax, sniffs and laughs.) Tiger bone and pine - the old herbalist has not forgotten me. Twenty years I walked the walls of Nanzhang, and now the rain decides when I may stand. Maybe not anymore. The next time the tigers come to the stakes, I will meet them on two good legs. Thank you, friend.
The salve is still in your pack. Jianshan keeps watch at the north gate of Mossgate, south-west of the city.
Your pack is too full for even one small jar. Make some room and come back.

quests.title: Shells on the Ledge Path
dialog: I came down from the mountains for silence. Up there the wind never stops talking; down here, I thought, only the fen would speak, and the fen speaks softly. Then the Bog Dragon Turtles found the path under my ledge - slow and stubborn - and the Venomspine Guivres followed them like crows follow a plough. Silence is never simply given, traveller. Someone has to win it back.

quests.title: Why do you live on the ledge?
dialog: Because from the ledge you can see everything, and nothing can see you. I spent thirty years in a monastery in the mountains, ringing a bell every morning. One day I realized I had never heard the silence between the strokes. So I came down, found this ledge above the fen and stayed. People climb past me on the ropes and ask if I am lonely. I tell them I have the fen, the wind and myself - and that is already one too many.

quests.title: Do you remember me?
dialog: The ledge path is mine again - I can sit and watch the fen without counting shells. Thank you, wanderer.

quests.title: Shells on the Ledge Path
quests.mission: Hunt 120 Bog Dragon Turtles; Hunt 80 Venomspine Guivres
dialog: I came down from the mountains for silence. Up there the wind never stops talking; down here, I thought, only the fen would speak, and the fen speaks softly. Then the Bog Dragon Turtles found the path under my ledge. They crawl up out of the marsh, slow and stubborn, and the Venomspine Guivres follow them like crows follow a plough. Clack, hiss, clack - all day long. Send them back to the bog: 120 turtles and 80 Venomspines. Then perhaps I can hear myself think again.
Thank you. The turtles come up from the marsh just below the cliff, and the Guivres are never far behind. Walk softly - for my sake.
Then I will sit and listen to the shells. It is a kind of meditation, I suppose. A very bad one.
Clack, hiss, clack. 120 turtles and 80 Venomspines - the path is not mine yet.
Your pack is too heavy for the cliff path. Make some room and come back.
Hear that? Neither do I. Only the wind in the reeds and a frog somewhere in the fen. That is all I ever wanted. Take this. A hermit has little use for coin - you will find a better one.
The ledge path is clear. Return to Hermit Bo Lin at the western cliff.

quests.title: Night Hunters
dialog: The tigers I can live with - they come, they test the stakes, they leave. The worst used to come after dark. Nightfang Guivres and Shadow Hydras hunt just beyond the reach of our lamps. They move without a sound, and you only see them when the light catches their eyes. These days they keep their distance - they have learned that Mossgate bites back.

quests.title: The Old Road
dialog: Mossgate was never just a village. It sits on the old road between the mine and Nanzhang - carts of ore went north, salt and rice came south, and every one of them stopped at our gate for water. For years the road belonged to the Mystic Bandits from the Old Mining Camp. They came down at night past the south gate, and on this knee I could never catch them. Now the carts are starting to come back. Slowly - but they come.

quests.title: Oil for the Night Watch
dialog: Every night one of us sits awake at a gate while the other sleeps. A watch without light is no watch at all - the tigers come right up to the stakes, and some nights they test them. We render lamp oil from the fat of the Poison Tigers; boiled long enough, the venom cooks out of it. Their gall is worth even more: dried and ground, it draws venom out of a wound and eases the ache in my knee when the rains come.

quests.title: Why did you leave the army?
dialog: I did not leave it - it left me. An arrow in the knee on a night patrol outside Nanzhang, and the next morning I was a soldier who could not march. They gave me a small purse and a big thank-you. Yuelan left with me. She could have stayed - hers was the best spear arm in our company. She said a wall is a wall, and she would rather guard one that is ours. So here we are: two old soldiers, a village of ruins and a fence of stakes.

quests.title: Do you remember me?
dialog: Stop there - ah, it is you. Come in. The stakes are for strangers, and you stopped being one a long time ago.

quests.title: Oil for the Night Watch
quests.mission: Collect 160 lumps of Poison Tiger Fat; Collect 80 Poison Tiger Galls
dialog: Every night one of us sits awake at a gate while the other sleeps. A watch without light is no watch at all - the tigers come right up to the stakes, and some nights they test them. We render lamp oil from the fat of the Poison Tigers; boiled long enough, the venom cooks out of it. Their gall is worth even more: dried and ground, it draws venom out of a wound and eases the ache in my knee when the rains come. Bring me one hundred and sixty lumps of fat and eighty galls. Only a hunter who cuts with purpose finds them - they will come to you once you agree.
Good. The Mystic Poison Tigers prowl beyond the south gate, along the old road to the mine. About one in five gives fat worth rendering, one in ten a whole gall.
No shame in that. Keep to the middle of the road - the stakes can cover you there.
Not enough yet. One hundred and sixty lumps of fat and eighty galls - one lamp at each gate, every night, until spring.
Your pack is too full for what I have for you. Make some room and come back.

That will keep both gates lit until spring, and my knee will thank you every time it rains. In Nanzhang I guarded walls that belonged to the lords. Here, for the first time, I guard something that is ours. Take this - and if the night is quiet, sit by our fire for a while.
You have the fat and the galls. Return to Hermit Jianshan Sima in Mossgate.

quests.title: Night Hunters
quests.mission: Hunt 120 Nightfang Guivres; Hunt 120 Shadow Hydras
dialog: The tigers I can live with - they come, they test the stakes, they leave. The worst comes after dark. Nightfang Guivres and Shadow Hydras hunt just beyond the reach of our lamps. They move without a sound, and you only see them when the light catches their eyes. Last week one of them took our goat from inside the fence. Stand the night watch with me. One hundred and twenty Guivres and one hundred and twenty Hydras - that should teach the rest to keep their distance.
Good. Keep the lamp at your back and your eyes on the dark. They hunt in the hollows around the village, a short walk beyond the palisade.
Then sleep inside the fence tonight, and do not open the gate for anything that knocks.
The dark is still full of eyes. One hundred and twenty Guivres and one hundred and twenty Hydras - keep at it.
Your pack is too full for what I have for you. Make some room and come back.

For the first time this season I sat the whole watch without gripping my spear. Even Yuelan slept through the night. In Nanzhang I stood watch with a whole company around me. Here it was only me and a lamp - until you came. Take this, watchman.
The night hunters are thinned out. Return to Hermit Jianshan Sima in Mossgate.

quests.title: The Old Road
quests.mission: Hunt 150 Mystic Bandits; Hunt 150 Mystic Bandit Archers
dialog: Mossgate was never just a village. It sits on the old road between the mine and Nanzhang - carts of ore went north, salt and rice came south, and every one of them stopped at our gate for water. Now the road belongs to the Mystic Bandits from the Old Mining Camp. They come down at night past the south gate, take what they can carry and are gone before I reach the stakes. On this knee I will never catch them. You can. Thin them out for me: one hundred and fifty Mystic Bandits and one hundred and fifty of their archers.
Good. They camp along the old road south of Mossgate, toward the mine. The archers stay back in the trees - deal with them first, or they will pin you to the road.
Then keep your purse close if you walk south. They are not picky about whose cart it is.
I still hear them on the road at night. One hundred and fifty bandits and one hundred and fifty archers - the road will not open by itself.
Your pack is too full for what I have for you. Make some room and come back.

The south gate was quiet all night - I did not even reach for my spear. Tomorrow I will send word to Nanzhang that the old road can carry carts again. Take this. Once the carts come back, Mossgate will be a village again, not just two old soldiers behind a fence.
The bandits are thinned out. Return to Hermit Jianshan Sima in Mossgate.

quests.title: Grave Goods
dialog: Behind the village, past the old wall, lie the barrows of Mossgate. My grandparents rest there - I cleaned their stones with my own hands the day we came back. Once the Mystic Bandits dug them open and took everything we had laid beside our dead: bowls, coins, jade amulets, while their leader told them where to dig. Every offering is back in its place now, and the barrows are sealed with stone.

quests.title: Hide and Sinew
dialog: Every stake in that fence I drove in myself, with this mallet. My husband held the walls of Nanzhang, and I held a spear right beside him. Life here is harder than any watch there - but it is ours. The roofs of Mossgate are covered with the thick hides of the Blood Tigers that hunt along the road, and the palisade is bound with their sinew: wound wet around a stake, it dries tighter than any rope.

quests.title: A Roof for the Tent Folk
dialog: When we left Nanzhang, we walked out through the south gate. Right under the walls there is a camp - people in tents, people under carts, people who cannot pay for a single night at an inn. The city takes their work and gives them canvas. Here we have houses with new roofs and work on the palisade. No rent, no taxes. Tinker Bao promised to bring the first families before the rains - and when children run through Mossgate again, it will be a village, not a ruin.

quests.title: Why rebuild a dead village?
dialog: Because it is not dead - it is sleeping. Our grandparents were born here, and our parents too, until Hu Lan came and everyone ran to Nanzhang. The city kept us alive, but it counted every coin and every day of our lives. Here nobody counts. Every roof I put back is one more family that could live here. I want to hear laughter between these walls before I am too old to swing a mallet. That is not a dead village. That is a promise.

quests.title: Do you remember me?
dialog: Look - two roofs now, and a third by spring. When children run through Mossgate again, they will hear your name.

quests.title: A Roof for the Tent Folk
quests.mission: Talk to Tinker Bao below the south gate of Nanzhang
dialog: When we left Nanzhang, we walked out through the south gate. Right under the walls there is a camp - people in tents, people under carts, people who cannot pay for a single night at an inn.
