Find an Explorer in the lands of Nanzhang and speak with her.
Make some room in your inventory and talk to me again.
So you have seen the wild places of Nanzhang with your own eyes. Good - a citizen should know what the city defends.
You have found an Explorer. Return to Palace Steward Bai Yun at the Imperial Palace.

quests.title: Pay the Tax
quests.mission: Pay the tax of 8,000,000 gold to Palace Steward Bai Yun
dialog: One last thing, and the most honest one: every citizen pays the city tax. Eight million gold - and the Emperor will seal your citizenship.
Keep the gold with you and talk to me when you are ready to pay.
Without the tax there is no citizenship. Come back when you are ready to pay.
You do not have 8,000,000 gold with you. Come back when you have it.
Make some room in your inventory and talk to me again.
The tax of a citizen of Nanzhang: 8,000,000 gold. Pay it now and the Emperor will seal your citizenship.
I cannot take your tax right now. Come back a little later.
The tax is paid. By decree of the Emperor, here is your citizenship of Nanzhang, signed and sealed. Read it carefully - and welcome, citizen.

quests.title: A Bet on Strangers
dialog: Tian Xiaoshu, the boy by the well, bet me his lucky river stone that no traveler would ever reach our gate again. He said I cheat, so he would not believe it from me. He had to see a traveler with his own eyes - and he did. The stone sits on my table now, and the boy has not stopped asking questions since.

quests.title: Do you ever lose a bet?
dialog: Lose? Ha! I lose all the time - that is the secret. Lose small and often, and people keep betting with you. Win big once, and they remember it for ten years. The only bet I ever truly feared was the one with Tian Xiaoshu - that no traveler would ever reach our gate again. Then you walked in. Some bets you win just by waiting long enough.

quests.title: Do you remember me?
dialog: My lucky traveler! Thanks to you that river stone sits on my table. Care for a new bet? No? Wise.

quests.title: A Bet on Strangers
dialog: Ha! Do you know what you are worth to me, stranger? Young Tian Xiaoshu bet me his lucky river stone that no traveler would ever reach our gate again. He will not believe it from me - he says I cheat. Go and let him see you with his own eyes. He is usually sitting by the fire near the well.
Off you go! And tell him Pan Laifu sends his regards.
A pity. The stone would have looked good on my table.
The boy is by the fire near the well. Go on, let him see you.

You are real! Pan Laifu won the stone... fine, fine, he can have it. But you have to tell me everything - the roads, the cities, the sea! Grandpa says I ask too many questions. I say there were never enough people to ask.
Go to Tian Xiaoshu by the fire near the well and let him see you.

quests.title: A Fish for the Ancestors
dialog: Before the families of Nanzhang burn incense for their ancestors, the offering table must hold a fish from living water - a sign that the river of life still flows for those who remember. That is the old custom. Fisherman Lao Heng keeps a hut by the lake west of the city, and he always knows what the fish is for. Nobody haggles with the dead.

quests.title: Bones for the Tombstones
dialog: Beyond the south wall lie the poor graves - mounds of earth that had no name and no stone. The stonemasons of old taught that tiger bone, ground and mixed into the mortar, makes a tombstone no restless spirit can break. The tigers around Nanzhang took many of those who lie there; it is only right that their bones guard the graves now. Every grave deserves a stone, and every stone a lantern.

quests.title: Who rests in this cemetery?
dialog: Everyone Nanzhang has ever loved and lost. Merchants and soldiers, potters and scholars, families who have burned incense here for twenty generations. Many came in a single season, when Hu Lan's beasts first came out of the forests. Under the old trees lies Lady Qiu Lan of the house of Dugu, who fled her manor and lived her last year in our city. And beyond the south wall rest the poor. Every lantern here burns for someone who is still remembered.

quests.title: Do you remember me?
dialog: You again. The nameless graves have their stones now, thanks to you. The ancestors are quieter at night - and so am I.

quests.title: A Fish for the Ancestors
quests.mission: Talk to Fisherman Lao Heng by the lake
dialog: Soon the families of Nanzhang will come to burn incense for their ancestors, and the offering table before the shrine is still bare. The old custom asks for a fish from living water - a sign that the river of life still flows for those who remember. Fisherman Lao Heng keeps a hut by the lake west of the city. Go to him and ask for a fish for the ancestors. He will know what it is for.
Follow the road west out of the city until you see the water. Lao Heng will be at the shore - he always is. Tell him that Chang Ming sent you.
The ancestors are patient. Come back when your road leads you here again.
You have not spoken with Lao Heng yet. The lake lies west of the city walls, past the old road.

A fish for Chang Ming's altar? Then it is for the ancestors, and nobody haggles with the dead. I pulled a fine silver carp out of the lake this morning - wait here, I will wrap it in fresh lotus leaves for you.
You have not spoken with Lao Heng yet. The lake lies west of the city walls, past the old road.

quests.title: Bones for the Tombstones
dialog: Beyond the south wall lie the poor graves - mounds of earth without a name and without a stone. Those people deserve to be remembered like everyone else. The stonemasons of old taught that tiger bone, ground and mixed into the mortar, makes a tombstone no restless spirit can break. The tigers that prowl around Nanzhang took many of those who lie there. Let their bones guard the graves now. Bring me six hundred tiger bones. They will come to you only once you take up this task.
Any tiger of the Nanzhang wilds will do - Mystic, Young, Blood, Frost or Poison. Three in four will leave a bone worth taking, never more than one. The stonemasons are waiting.
I understand. It is a heavy task. The graves have waited this long; they can wait a little longer.
Not enough yet. Six hundred bones - one tombstone needs many, and there are many graves without a name.
Your pack is too full for what I have for you. Make some room and come back.

Six hundred bones... The stonemasons will grind them at dawn, and by the next festival every nameless grave will have its stone. The families will light lanterns there as well. And somewhere among those lights there will be one for you, traveler. May the ancestors walk beside you.
You have the bones. Return to Priest Chang Ming at the cemetery in Nanzhang.

quests.title: How is the library coming along?
dialog: The first sacks of rice went to the library square this morning. Builders eat like tigers - I have never sold so much salt in my life.

quests.title: The Library of Nanzhang
dialog: The library? I was a boy when it burned. My father sold lamp oil to the scholars - he said they read until the oil ran out, and then argued in the dark. Ledger Keeper Shen keeps the books that survived.

A library for Nanzhang? Then the builders will need to eat. Rice, oil, salt, rope and lamp wicks - my stores will feed every worker on that square until the last roof tile is laid. Tell Lady Shen she has the word of Gu Wan.
You have won the support of Provisioner Gu Wan.
You have won the support of Provisioner Gu Wan.  Quest complete: Patrons of the Library. Return to Ledger Keeper Shen to receive your reward.
Quest complete: Patrons of the Library. Return to Ledger Keeper Shen to receive your reward.

quests.title: The Paths Must Stay Open
dialog: Our people used to walk to the lake and to the old shrine without fear. Then every path out of the village became a hunting ground. The Dreadmaws lie in wait by the water and on the shrine path, and the Poison Tigers stalk the forest north of the village. Since a traveler thinned them out, the bearers come home without a scratch.

quests.title: How long has the village been hidden?
dialog: Twenty winters since a stranger last stood before my house. Longer since we stopped walking the roads. When Hu Lan and his horde burned the woods, the white mist came down over our fences, and their fire never found us. My father said the gods remembered our offerings. We have carried them to the shrine every day since - and now the forest sends us travelers again. I think the gods are telling us something.

quests.title: Do you remember me?
dialog: The bearers walk to the shrine singing now. Singing! Twenty winters I waited to hear that. Sit, traveler - you are one of us.

quests.title: The Paths Must Stay Open
quests.mission: Hunt 80 Dreadmaws; Hunt 80 Mystic Poison Tigers
dialog: Our people used to walk to the lake and to the old shrine without fear. Now every path out of the village is a hunting ground. The Dreadmaws lie in wait by the water and on the shrine path, and the Poison Tigers stalk the forest north of the village. Thin them out for us: eighty Dreadmaws and eighty Poison Tigers. Will you do this for an old man?
Thank you. Hunt them along the paths around the village - to the lake in the north and to the shrine in the south-west.
I understand. The forest has taken braver men than you. Rest here while you can.
The paths are still not safe. I can hear the beasts from my porch every night.
Your pack is too full for what I have for you. Make some room and come back.
Tonight the bearers came back from the shrine without a single scratch. I have not seen that in years. Take this - it is little, but it comes from the whole village.
The paths are clear for now. Return to Qian Shoushan in the Forgotten Village.

quests.title: Who is the stone general by the gate?
quests.mission: Conversation with Retired General Zhao Heng
dialog: A general of the old wars - I served under him as a boy. The sculptor gave him a stern face, which is unfair: he laughed at everything and could not hold his wine. I salute him every morning. He has never once saluted back.

quests.title: Trust the Knots
dialog: Everyone asks if they can trust my knots. The knots, yes; the rope is another question. Hemp rots in the damp of the Venom Fen - one wet season, and a rope that held an ox snaps under a traveller. The sinew of a Venomspine Guivre does not rot and does not tear. Braided into the hemp, it makes a rope that will outlive us both. That is the only rope I hang on this wall now.

quests.title: Should I trust your knots?
dialog: Trust the knot more than the cliff, and the rope more than your own hands. I have tied knots since I was old enough to hold a cord - my father hauled salt up this wall before there was any road. Every morning I check each rope from top to bottom, and every evening once more. Nobody has fallen from my ropes. One man fell from his own pride, trying to climb without them. Hold on, do not look down, and never argue with the rope.

quests.title: Do you remember me?
dialog: Every rope on this wall is braided with the sinew you brought. Climb as often as you like - for you there is no fee.

quests.title: Trust the Knots
dialog: Everyone asks if they can trust my knots. The knots, yes. The rope - that is another question. Hemp rots in the damp of the Venom Fen. One wet season, and a rope that held an ox snaps under a traveller. But the sinew of a Venomspine Guivre does not rot and does not tear - braid it into the hemp and the rope will outlive us both. Bring me 40 Venomspine sinews. Only a clean cut gives sinew worth braiding, so they will come to you only once you agree.
Good. The Guivres crawl in the Venom Fen, a short walk from this cliff where the marsh begins. About one in five will give you a sinew long enough for a rope.
Then I will check the old ropes twice before every climb. Three times, maybe.
Not 40 yet. I do not braid a rope halfway - and I do not let anyone climb a rope braided halfway.
Your pack is too full for what I have for you. Make some room and come back.

Look at that - pull as hard as you like, it will not give. The new ropes go up this week, and the old ones go on the fire where they belong. Take this. And trust my knots, friend - you made half of them.
You have the sinew. Return to Ropemaster Gao Shan at the eastern cliff.

quests.title: Venom for the Spirit Rite
dialog: Incense, herbs and old bones I can buy in the market. But the one ingredient that truly opens the way is venom - the venom of the Mystic Poison Tigers. A few drops in the censer, and the smoke carries a voice from the other side: a last word from a father, a goodbye from a wife. Few hunters dare to go after those beasts, and fewer still come back with the venom unspoiled.

quests.title: Can you really speak with the dead?
dialog: Speak? No. The dead speak; I only listen, and the smoke carries their words to the living. Not every spirit answers. Some have gone too far, some are angry, and some are simply lost - they wander and cannot find their way back to the ones who call them. For those, a name helps. Say a name over my censer, and a lost spirit can follow it home like a lantern in the dark. That is why people bring me names more often than coins.

quests.title: Do you remember me?
dialog: The spirits know your face now, traveler. When you brought the venom, the smoke carried more than one voice home.

quests.title: Emerald Dragon Flag
quests.mission: Phial of Ancient Beast's Blood from Xiong the Great
dialog: I can help you create an Emerald Dragon Flag. But besides the Pure Dragon Flag I need the blood of an ancient, dark beast - Xiong the Great. Kill Xiong the Great and bring me his blood. We need it for the ritual.
You do not have to kill him alone - if someone in your party kills him, the blood will be yours too. Share experience and items in your party and stay close.
Then the flag stays pure... and powerless. Come back when you are ready to hunt.
I still need the blood of Xiong the Great. Kill him and bring me the Phial.
Make some room in your inventory and come back.
The blood of the ancient beast... I can feel its strength through the glass. Now I have everything I need for the ritual.
You have the Phial of Ancient Beast's Blood. Return to Shamaness Yue in Nanzhang.

quests.title: Blessing of Huang Long
quests.mission: Give the Pure Dragon Flag to Shamaness Yue and come back after midnight (daily reset)
quests.rewards: Experience 49662021 / SP 4000 / Emerald Dragon Flag (Str +5, Int +5, Damage +1%) / Emerald Dragon Flag attachment (Menu > Outfit)
dialog: Now the Pure Dragon Flag must be filled with the essence of Huang Long. Only a ritual can do that, and only at night. Will you give me your flag for the ritual?
Give me the Pure Dragon Flag when you are ready.
Keep it then. Come back when you are ready.
The ritual is not finished yet. Come back tomorrow.
Make some room in your inventory for the flag and talk to me again.
Huang Long was willing. The ritual is complete - take your flag.
The spirits are silent right now. Come back a little later.
Give me your Pure Dragon Flag. I will perform the ritual tonight.
I must fill the flag with the essence of Huang Long, our dragon - if he is willing. I will perform the ritual tonight. Come back tomorrow.
I must perform the ritual. If the dragon is willing to help, you can come back to me tomorrow.
Here is your Emerald Dragon Flag. The Emerald Dragon Flag attachment is waiting for you in Menu > Outfit.
You do not have the Pure Dragon Flag with you. Bring it in your inventory.

quests.title: Venom for the Spirit Rite
quests.mission: Collect 160 flasks of Poison Tiger Venom
dialog: Incense, herbs and old bones I can buy in the market. But the one ingredient that truly opens the way is venom - the venom of the Mystic Poison Tigers. A few drops in the censer, and the smoke carries a voice from the other side. Few hunters dare to go after those beasts, and fewer come back with the venom unspoiled. Bring me one hundred and sixty flasks of Poison Tiger Venom. It will come to you only once you agree.
The Mystic Poison Tigers prowl the Ashen Fields and the Forest of Whispers, south of the city. Roughly one in five will give venom worth keeping - seal it quickly, before it loses its strength.
Then the dead will wait a little longer. They are patient - more patient than the living.
Not yet. One hundred and sixty flasks - every family that comes to me deserves one more word from their dead.
Your pack is too full for what I have for you. Make some room and come back.

The smoke will be thick with voices tonight. A widow from the lower market has waited all season to speak with her husband once more - now she can. The spirits remember those who help them. Take this, and if one day you need to hear someone you have lost, you know where to find me.
You have the venom. Return to Shamaness Yue in Nanzhang.

quests.title: Pelts Before the Frost
dialog: Winter in this forest is cruel. One year two of the children fell sick from the cold, and our blankets were worn thin. The pelts of the Poison Tigers are thick and warm - once the poison is washed out of them. I know how to do it, and now nobody in the village sleeps cold.

quests.title: Will the merchants come back?
dialog: I count the stores every evening - grain, salt, blankets, needles. Salt and needles we cannot make ourselves, and the last of them came through the mist twenty winters ago. If travelers like you can find our gate, merchants can too. I have already cleared a corner of the storehouse for them. The elder says I hope too much. I say somebody in this village has to.

quests.title: Do you remember me?
dialog: The children asked who the warm blankets came from. I told them: from a traveler who came through the mist. Now they wait for you at the gate.

quests.title: Pelts Before the Frost
dialog: Winter in this forest is cruel, and our blankets are worn thin. Last year two of the children fell sick from the cold. The pelts of the Poison Tigers are thick and warm - once the poison is washed out of them. I know how to do it. Bring me thirty pelts. They are only good if cut carefully, so they will come to you only once you agree to help me.
Thank you! The Poison Tigers prowl the forest north of the village. About one in three pelts will be whole.
Oh... then I will patch the old blankets once more.
Thirty pelts, no fewer - I have counted every bed in the village.
Your pack is too full for what I have for you. Make some room and come back.
Thirty! Every child in the village will sleep warm this winter. Take this from our stores - and tell the merchants out there that the Forgotten Village pays its debts.
You have the pelts. Return to Shen Yuzhu by the storehouse.

quests.title: What is the evil in the mountain?
quests.mission: Conversation with Shrine Keeper Hui Jing
dialog: I have prayed over it for years and I still have no name for it. It is not fire and it is not smoke. It is cold, even when it rises from the hot cracks, and it makes the dogs howl and the old ones dream of the dead. It came with Hu Lan, and it feeds on the anger of the mountain.

quests.title: Does the shrine protect the village?
quests.mission: Conversation with Shrine Keeper Hui Jing
dialog: A little. Every evening I draw a line of salt around the houses and burn incense at the four corners. The smoke from the cracks drifts toward Kuhe, turns and goes around us. I do not know how long such small things will hold, but so far they have.

quests.title: Do you remember me?
quests.mission: Conversation with Shrine Keeper Hui Jing
dialog: Salt, incense and a stranger's help - three small things against one mountain. So far they hold.

quests.title: The Village in the Mist
quests.mission: Conversation with Shrine Keeper Hui Ming
dialog: Deeper in the forest, behind a wall of white mist, there is a village - the Forgotten Village. Everything else in these woods fell to Hu Lan and his horde, yet that village still stands. Every day its people carry offerings to this shrine, and the mist keeps them hidden. Once the path stayed empty for a whole day, and I could not leave the shrine to find out why. A traveler went for me.

quests.title: Who built this shrine?
quests.mission: Conversation with Shrine Keeper Hui Ming
dialog: Nobody remembers. It stood here before the Forgotten Village had a name, before Nanzhang had walls. Some say the first villagers found it already old, and chose to settle near it. I only keep it. I sweep the steps, light the incense and wait for the bearers. The shrine does not need a builder anymore. It needs someone who comes back every morning.

quests.title: Do you remember me?
quests.mission: Conversation with Shrine Keeper Hui Ming
dialog: The offerings arrive every morning again. I light a stick of incense for the one who walked into the mist for strangers.

quests.title: The Village in the Mist
quests.mission: Talk to Yuanjue in the Forgotten Village
dialog: You came along the old road? Then listen. Deeper in the forest, behind a wall of white mist, there is a village - the Forgotten Village. Everything else in these woods fell to Hu Lan and his horde, yet that village still stands. Every day its people carry offerings to this shrine. Today no one came, and I cannot leave the shrine unguarded. Go to the village and find the monk Yuanjue. Tell him the offerings did not arrive.
Follow the old path east through the forest until the air turns white. Yuanjue stands by the bell, near the well.
Then may the gods keep you on your road. I will keep waiting.
The monk Yuanjue is waiting in the Forgotten Village. Follow the path east.

Hui Ming sent you? Then the offerings never reached the shrine... I feared as much. Listen, traveler. The white mist you walked through is no ordinary fog. It is a gift of the gods who guard this village. Hu Lan and his horde destroyed everything around these woods - the village beyond the Mirk Woods, the one where only a witch's fire still burns. But their eyes never found us. The mist hides us. The gods ask little in return: an offering at the shrine, every day. Take this for your trouble - and speak with me again.
Go to the Forgotten Village and speak with the monk Yuanjue. The path east will lead you there.

quests.title: How is silk made?
quests.mission: Conversation with Silk Merchant Madam Wen Xiu
dialog: With worms, believe it or not - thousands of them, fed on mulberry leaves day and night. Each cocoon gives one thread longer than this street. My weavers twist eight together, then the dyers take over: red from madder root, gold from pagoda tree flowers, blue from indigo. One good bolt takes a whole season.

quests.title: Who buys your silk?
quests.mission: Conversation with Silk Merchant Madam Wen Xiu
dialog: Everyone who can afford it, and many who cannot. Officials need robes for court, brides need red for their weddings, and merchants from Constantinople pay in gold for a single bolt. They carry it west and sell it for ten times more. I call it robbery. They call it trade.

quests.title: How is the library coming along?
quests.mission: Conversation with Silk Merchant Mei Lin
dialog: My seamstresses are already cutting silk for the new spines. River-pearl blue, as promised.

quests.title: The Library of Nanzhang
dialog: A library? There was one, before my time - by the Lotus Garden. Silk carries stories along the roads, but books keep them. Ask Ledger Keeper Shen; she knows more.
Books for Nanzhang? Then my workshop will bind them. Silk for the spines, river-pearl blue - a library dressed better than half the merchants in this square. Tell Lady Shen she has me.
I have promised already - silk for the spines. Run along and tell Lady Shen.

quests.title: When the Stars Are Restless
dialog: Three red stars once climbed over the south-east, and none of them was in my almanac. When the sky is uneasy, the beasts in the forest are too: that same month the Abyssal Dragon Turtles crawled out of the deep water south-east of the city, dozens of them, led by one far bigger than the rest. The sky and the earth answer each other. I only write down what they say.

quests.title: What do the stars say?
dialog: Tonight? That the Golden Dragon still watches over Nanzhang - see the bright one there, above the palace roofs? As long as it burns, the city stands. But for a month I have been drawing stars that are in no almanac. Some climb over the forests and fade within a week. Some burn red. The old books say a new star means something has woken that should have stayed asleep. Since Hu Lan, much has woken. I only write it down.

quests.title: Do you remember me?
dialog: The sky has been calm for nine nights. I wrote your name in my star book, beside the omen you silenced.

quests.title: When the Stars Are Restless
quests.mission: Hunt 150 Abyssal Dragon Turtles; Slay 1 Abyssal Dragon Turtle Champion
dialog: The stars were restless again last night. Three red stars climbed over the south-east, and none of them is in my almanac. When the sky is uneasy, the beasts in the forest are too. I went to look, and the sky was right to worry: Abyssal Dragon Turtles have crawled out of the deep water south-east of the city - dozens of them, and one far bigger than the rest. Thin them out, a hundred and fifty of them, and slay the great one. If I am right, the sky will calm down with them.
Leave the city and keep to the south-east - the turtles lie along the shore of the deep water. The great one keeps to the middle of the herd.
Then I will keep watching. Someone has to write down what the sky says, even if no one listens.
The red stars still burn over the south-east. A hundred and fifty turtles and the great one - the omen is not answered yet.
Your pack is too full for what I have for you. Make some room and come back.

Look - there, over the south-east. Two of the red stars have faded, and the third is only a spark. The omen is answered. Tonight I will write it in my star book: the night the sky grew calm, and why. Take this, traveler.
The turtles are thinned. Return to Sky-Reader Tan in the garden behind the temple of Nanzhang.

quests.title: How do six men hold a gate?
dialog: With towers, smoke and a bad temper. There are two towers on the palisade and a smoke pot on each. When the buzzing starts, the man at the gate rings the bell and we all run up. Smoke makes the Ongs dizzy, and a dizzy Ong is an easy target. We sleep in turns, eat in turns and complain all together. The captain says six is enough. The captain sleeps on his boat.

quests.title: Do you remember me?
dialog: At ease, friend - the swarm has not tested this gate since you thinned it. The towers are yours whenever you need them.

quests.title: Six Against the Swarm
dialog: Six of us hold this gate against the swarm. When the buzzing starts, we run for the towers and light the smoke pots - smoke confuses them, arrows do the rest. For a long time the swarm grew bigger every week, and the hives on the ridge kept swelling. We knew that one day they would come over the palisade all at once, and six men do not stop that. Thanks to a stranger, that day has not come.

quests.title: Six Against the Swarm
dialog: Six of us hold this gate against the swarm. Six. When the buzzing starts, we run for the towers and light the smoke pots - smoke confuses them, arrows do the rest. But every week the swarm is bigger. The hives on the ridge are swelling, and one day they will come over the palisade all at once. Six men do not stop that. Thin them before they try: 250 Bloodwings and 250 Dreadwings. It is a big job. That is why I am asking you and not the cook.
Good. The hives are all over the ridge around the landing - step outside the palisade and they will find you first. Keep your back to the rocks and do not stop moving.
Fair enough. If you hear buzzing, run for the towers like the rest of us.
The ridge is still humming. 250 Bloodwings and 250 Dreadwings, friend - the palisade will not hold forever.
Your pack is full, friend. Lighten it, then report back to me.

Last night the bell stayed silent for the first time since I came here. The others think I made a deal with the ridge. Take this - the six of us put it together. And if you ever need a tower to sleep in, there is always one free.
The swarm is thinned. Return to Soldier Liang Chong at the palisade gate of Hive Ridge Landing.

quests.title: What do people send across the water?
dialog: Everything a family cannot carry itself. Letters, mostly - sons in Hotan writing to mothers in Kuhe, and sometimes mothers writing back. Silver wrapped in cloth, seeds, a pair of shoes for a grandson, medicine from the city. Once a whole wedding dress, folded so small I could not believe it. I never open them. A parcel is a promise, and a promise travels with its knot unbroken.

quests.title: Do you remember me?
dialog: Every knot counted, every parcel home - and half of them thanks to you. You may peek inside one. Just one.

quests.title: Every Knot Counted
dialog: One of my porters never reached the landing. The Dreadwings caught him on the cliff path and dragged the parcels to their nests, as if they were something to eat. Whole families had trusted me with them - letters, silver for parents, medicine. I count every knot that leaves this landing, and I counted every knot that came back. No parcel is lost while I sit on this bundle.

quests.title: Every Knot Counted
dialog: My porter never reached the landing. The Dreadwings caught him on the cliff path and tore him apart - and then they dragged the parcels off to their nests, as if they were something to eat. Whole families trusted me with those parcels. Letters, silver for parents, medicine. I count every knot that leaves this landing, and I will count every knot that comes back. Bring me 40 of them. I know my knots - do not try to sell me any others.
Thank you. The Dreadwings nest along the cliff path beyond the palisade. About one in five has one of my parcels stuck in its nest - you will know them by the double knot.
Then I will have to write to every family that their parcel is lost. No. I will wait a little longer.
Not 40 yet. I have the list right here - every parcel, every knot.
Your pack is too full for what I have for you. Make some room and come back.

Let me see... double knot, red cord - that is the silver for the tailor's mother. And this one, the medicine for Kuhe. All still sealed! Take this, with my thanks. The next boat leaves full, and nobody will ever know how close their parcels came to an Ong's nest.
You have the parcels. Return to Tang Cuiping by the parcels at Hive Ridge Landing.

quests.title: How is the library coming along?
dialog: I am choosing the tea for the reading hall. Something misty and slow - books should not be rushed.

quests.title: The Library of Nanzhang
dialog: The old library? As an apprentice I brought tea to the scholars there. They argued all day and read until the lamps burned out. Ledger Keeper Shen keeps the books now.
Sit, breathe... a library, you say? A library without a tea room is only a storehouse. I will pay for the reading hall - on condition that the tea is mine. Tell Lady Shen.
I have promised the reading hall already. Tell Lady Shen - and bring her a cup from me.

quests.title: What tea are you drinking?
quests.mission: Conversation with Tea Master Qian Boyan
dialog: White peony from the southern hills. The leaves are picked before sunrise, while the dew is still on them, and dried in the shade so they keep their sweetness. One cup at dawn, one at dusk. More than that and you are only drinking hot water with ambitions.

quests.title: Why are you always at this table?
quests.mission: Conversation with Tea Master Qian Boyan
dialog: From this table I see the whole square: who walks with whom, who bows to whom, whose servants carry the heaviest baskets. Half of the deals in this district are made over a cup of tea. The other half are broken over the second cup.

quests.title: What lies beyond the mist?
dialog: I don't know! That's the problem. Grandpa Qian says there is only fire and tigers out there. Pan Laifu says there are cities with walls taller than the trees, and markets bigger than our whole village. Shen Yuzhu says there are merchants with needles. You came from out there, so you know. One day I will walk into the mist and keep walking until I see it myself. But don't tell Grandpa. He worries.

quests.title: Do you remember me?
dialog: You came back! Tell me again about the walls taller than the trees. Grandpa says I ask too much, but you never mind.

quests.title: Why do you sleep under canvas?
dialog: Because canvas costs nothing and the inns cost everything. One night in the cheapest inn of Nanzhang is more than I earn mending pots in a week. So I sleep here, under the south gate, with the others like me - carters without carts, farmers without farms, all of us waiting for something better. My own village burned when I was a boy. A tinker can mend a kettle, but not a roof he does not have.

quests.title: Do you remember me?
dialog: Mossgate, eh? A roof without rent and a gate that needs hinges... You may have mended more than an old pot, friend.

quests.title: What brings a trader to Kuhe?
dialog: The new trade road. Caravans now come up from Hive Ridge Landing Ferry and cross the dry river here instead of going around the ridge. It saves them two days. Two days means water, fodder and a roof for the night - and Kuhe is the only roof for many miles.

quests.title: What do you trade here?
dialog: Salt and cloth from the ferry, tea and iron from the south. From the mountain - black glass, sulphur and a red stone that the jewellers of Hotan pay well for. The villagers dig it at dawn, when the slopes are quiet. Strange, is it not? The same mountain that ruined them may yet make them rich.

quests.title: Toll Without a Gate
dialog: The new road saves a caravan two days - and for a while the Mystic Bandits from the old mines took back three days' profit. They sat by the road south of the village and collected a toll without a gate: pay, or lose the mules. Two caravans turned back that month, and a caravan that turns back does not come again. On a trade road, fear costs more than any toll.

quests.title: Do you remember me?
dialog: My best customer! No, no, you pay nothing today - a road without bandits is worth more than any discount.

quests.title: Toll Without a Gate
quests.mission: Hunt 150 Mystic Bandits; Hunt 150 Mystic Bandit Archers; Slay 1 Mystic Bandit Archer Champion
dialog: Ha! You look like someone who can count. Then count this: the new road saves a caravan two days - and the Mystic Bandits from the old mines take back three days' profit. They sit by the road south of the village and collect a toll without a gate. Pay, or lose the mules. Two caravans turned back last month, and a caravan that turns back does not come again. Break their toll: 150 Mystic Bandits, 150 Mystic Bandit Archers and the champion archer who leads them. Do this, and the merchants will keep coming.
Splendid! They watch the road from the rocks south of Kuhe, toward the old mining camp. The champion archer is the one in front - you will know him by the arrows that never miss.
Pity. Then I will raise my prices and blame the bandits - everyone does.
The toll is still being collected, friend. 150 Mystic Bandits, 150 Archers and their champion - then we talk business.
Your bags are bursting - even a trader knows when a cart is overloaded. Make some room first.

A caravan came through this morning, and not one copper went to a man in the rocks! My abacus has never been so happy. Take this - an honest share of an honest profit. And tell everyone you meet: the road through Kuhe is open.
The bandits' toll is broken. Return to Trader He Fu on the square of Kuhe Village.

quests.title: How did you walk that dangerous road alone?
dialog: Alone? Oh, sweetheart... do you need some company? It is a longer story, and I would gladly tell it to you somewhere else.

quests.title: Nanzhang Inventory Expansion
quests.mission: Collect 10 Shadow Hydra Skins; Collect 10 Nightfang Guivre Scales; Collect 10 Venom Hydra Skins; Collect 10 Venomspine Guivre Poisons; Collect 10 Bog Dragon Turtle Shells; Collect 10 Abyssal Dragon Turtle Blood; Collect 10 Magma Cyclops Eyes
quests.rewards: Experience 49662021 / SP 8000 / Inventory: 3rd page (if already unlocked: 5,000,000 Gold)
dialog: Oh my, look at your bag. It is about to burst at the seams! A hunter who roams the wilds around Nanzhang needs far more room than that. I know a tailor in the city who sews the finest travel bags in the empire - but he works only with rare materials. Bring me 10 Shadow Hydra Skins, 10 Nightfang Guivre Scales, 10 Venom Hydra Skins, 10 Venomspine Guivre Poisons, 10 Bog Dragon Turtle Shells, 10 Abyssal Dragon Turtle Blood and 10 Magma Cyclops Eyes. In return your bag will get a third page. If your bag is already as large as it can be, I will pay you for your trouble instead. Will you do it?

Wonderful. Shadow Hydras and Nightfang Guivres live in Mirk Woods and Dusk Forest south of the city, Abyssal Dragon Turtles in the Gloom Swamps. Venom Hydras and Venomspine Guivres lurk in the Blightwood, Bog Dragon Turtles in the Venom Fen north of the city, and Magma Cyclopes roam the slopes of Chiyan Volcano. Not every beast will give you what the tailor needs - about one in five.
As you wish. Come back when your bag starts to tear.
The tailor needs 10 of each material - no less. The beasts are still out there, go back.
Your bag is full. Make some room and talk to me again.

All the materials, and in fine condition! The tailor will be delighted. Here, let me fasten the new bag for you myself - check your inventory, it now has a third page. If your bag was already as large as it can be, take this gold for your trouble instead.
You have collected all the materials. Return to Warehouse Keeper Lan Yue at the Nanzhang Imperial Bank.

quests.title: Poison in the Springs
dialog: The wells of Nanzhang drink from springs that run under the ground from the north, from the Venom Fen. When the Venom Hydras and the Venomspine Guivres spread across the fen, their venom seeped into the water, and every day it tasted more bitter. A diviner learns to taste such things before anyone falls sick. Water cleans itself, if you only stop the poison at its source.

quests.title: How do you find water?
dialog: I listen. Put your ear to the ground at night and you will hear it too, if you are patient: a slow murmur, deeper than a heartbeat. Then I walk with my staff until it trembles in my hand, and there we dig. The rest is taste. Every spring tastes of the land it ran through - stone, roots, salt, sometimes ash. The wells of Nanzhang drink from the north, and I know each one by its taste, the way you know a friend by his voice.

quests.title: Do you remember me?
dialog: The springs run clean again - I can taste it. Water always finds the one who listens, and this time it found you.

quests.title: Poison in the Springs
quests.mission: Hunt 120 Venom Hydras; Hunt 120 Venomspine Guivres
dialog: Taste this. No? Wise. I have tasted it for a week, and every day it is more bitter. The wells of Nanzhang drink from springs that run under the ground from the north, from the Venom Fen. The Venom Hydras and the Venomspine Guivres have spread across the fen, and their venom is seeping into the water. A little more, and the first well will turn. Go north and thin them out - a hundred and twenty hydras and a hundred and twenty guivres. The water will clean itself; it only needs the poison to stop.
Leave by the north gate. The fen starts a short walk beyond the walls - you will smell it before you see it.
Then I will keep tasting. Someone has to know the day it turns.
Still bitter. The hydras and the guivres still crowd the fen - a hundred and twenty of each.
Your pack is too full for what I have for you. Make some room and come back.

(Anji draws a bucket from the well and drinks deeply.) Sweet. Cold and sweet, the way it should be. The springs are already washing themselves clean. Water always finds the one who listens - and today it found you. Take this, with the thanks of every well in Nanzhang.
The fen is thinned. Return to Water Diviner Anji in the granary yard of Nanzhang.

quests.title: Why build a landing here?
dialog: Because this is the only place for many miles where the cliffs come down to the water. Across it lies the Southern-Tarim Ferry and the road to Hotan; behind us, the road to Kuhe and on to Nanzhang. A caravan that crosses here saves weeks around the ridge. Yes, the hives were here first. We built the palisade, hired six soldiers and stayed. A landing nobody dares to build is a landing somebody else will build.

quests.title: Do you remember me?
dialog: The hive on the ridge lost its queen, and my boats lost their fear. Welcome back to Hive Ridge Landing.

quests.title: The Queen of the Ridge
dialog: The Bloodwings on the ridge are bigger than a man, and the biggest of them led the rest - the queen of the ridge. She never flew alone; the swarm and a champion Dreadwing guarded her flank. Her mandible hangs over the gate now, longer than my arm, where every boat can see it. A sign that this landing is not afraid.

quests.title: The Queen of the Ridge
quests.mission: Take 1 Hive Queen Mandible from the giant Bloodwing; Hunt 100 Bloodwings; Slay 1 Dreadwing Champion
dialog: You thinned the swarm - Liang Chong has not stopped talking about it. But the hive on the ridge still has its queen. The Bloodwings up there are bigger than a man, and the biggest of them leads the rest. Kill her. Bring me her mandible, and I will hang it over the gate where every boat can see it - a sign that this landing is not afraid. She never flies alone, so cut down 100 Bloodwings around her, and the champion Dreadwing that guards her flank.
Good. She keeps to the highest hives on the ridge - a giant among giants. Her mandible will not come from a common Bloodwing, only from her.
Then the boats will keep coming in fast and leaving faster. It is no way to run a landing.
The queen still rules the ridge. Bring me her mandible, and cut down 100 Bloodwings and the champion Dreadwing.
Your pack is too full for what I have for you. Make some room and come back.

So this is what she carried... it is longer than my arm. Tomorrow it goes up over the gate, and the captains will see it from the water. Take this. A landing is only as strong as the nerve of its boats - and today you gave this one its nerve back.
The queen is dead. Return to Wei Guanghai on the quay of Hive Ridge Landing.

quests.title: Why is the well so deep?
quests.mission: Conversation with Well Keeper Xiao Lian
dialog: When the river dried up, we followed the water down. My grandfather dug this well to the height of six men; we have dug it to forty. Down there it is black as a moonless night, and on still evenings you can hear the mountain rumbling far below. It is the last water in Kuhe.

quests.title: Is the water safe to drink?
quests.mission: Conversation with Well Keeper Xiao Lian
dialog: It tastes of ash and iron, but it is clean - I boil every bucket and the shrine keeper blesses the rope. Some nights the water comes up warm in the bucket. On those nights I let nobody drink until morning.

quests.title: Stingers on the Pass Road
dialog: This road through the pass is the only way down from the Tarim Basin, and I am paid to keep it open. Bandits I can handle; sand I can handle. Scorpions are another matter. The red ones crawl out of the dunes and sting the camels while they rest - one week we lost two animals, and a driver has walked with a limp ever since. Keep to the road, traveller, and never sit down in the sand.

quests.title: Why does the road need a warden?
dialog: Because the desert does not care about roads. One storm and the track is buried; one careless driver and a whole caravan follows him into the dunes. I mark the way with stones, I count who goes down and who comes up, and I send riders after anyone who does not arrive. Before the ferry, nobody walked this pass. Now half of Hotan's silk comes down it, and somebody has to make sure it reaches the water.

quests.title: Do you remember me?
dialog: The pass road is safe enough for children now - well, almost. I owe you a cup of something strong.

quests.title: Stingers on the Pass Road
quests.mission: Hunt 50 Small Red Scorpions; Hunt 50 Red Scorpions
dialog: This road through the pass is the only way down from the Tarim Basin, and I am paid to keep it open. Bandits I can handle. Sand I can handle. Scorpions I cannot. The red ones crawl out of the dunes and sting the camels while they rest - two animals lost this week, and a driver who will walk with a limp for the rest of his life. Clear the dunes along the road: 50 Small Red Scorpions and 50 Red Scorpions. Then the camels can rest in peace.
Good. They live in the dunes along the pass road, above the ferry. Watch your boots - the small ones are faster than they look.
Then keep to the road and do not sit down in the sand. Ever.
Still stingers on my road. 50 Small Red Scorpions and 50 Red Scorpions - I am counting the camels, not the hours.
Your pack is full. Make some room, then come back to the ferry.
Not one camel stung since yesterday - the drivers have started to sing again, which I could live without. Take this. The road is mine to guard, but today you guarded it better.
The dunes are quieter. Return to Wen Kuanglie on the pass road above the Southern-Tarim Ferry.

quests.title: What is in your chest?
dialog: His winter coat, two bowls, the comb he carved for me on our wedding day, and the deed to a house the moneylender has already taken. I sit on it at night, so nobody takes the rest.

quests.title: Where is your family?
dialog: My husband is buried behind the house. My sons took the road to the ferry three winters ago. The elder lives in Hotan now and works for a silk merchant; the younger went on to Donwhang. They send letters with the caravans, and every letter asks me to come. I read them twice and put them in the box.

quests.title: Why did so many people leave?
dialog: Because life here became hard. The fields give dust, the well gives a bucket a day, and the nights bring things nobody wants to see. Half the houses in Kuhe stand empty. People did not leave because they stopped loving this place. They left because they wanted their families to live.

quests.title: Letters in the Box
dialog: My sons write from Hotan and Donwhang, and every letter says the same: Mother, come to us. For three winters I read each one twice and put it in the box. I never answered - what could I write? That the river is gone and the house is quiet? Then one night I wrote: that I am well, that the roofs are being mended, that I miss them. Tang Cuiping put it on the boat herself.

quests.title: Do you remember me?
dialog: A letter came back from Hotan! My elder boy says he will visit when the roofs are done. Thank you for carrying my words.

quests.title: Letters in the Box
quests.mission: Deliver the Letter to Hotan to Tang Cuiping
dialog: My sons write from Hotan and Donwhang. Every letter says the same: Mother, come to us. I read each one twice and put it in the box with the others. I never answered. What could I write? That the river is gone and the house is quiet? But last night I wrote. Not much - that I am well, that the roofs are being mended, that I miss them. Tang Cuiping packs the parcels for the boat at Hive Ridge Landing. Would you take my letter to her?
Thank you. Here it is - mind the corner, I folded it too many times. The landing is north of here, along the trade road. Tang Cuiping sits on her bundle by the parcels; she will see it onto the boat.
No, of course. It waited three winters in my head - it can wait a little longer.
The letter is still with you? Tang Cuiping is at Hive Ridge Landing, by the parcels for the boat.

A letter from Kuhe? From Mei Hua? Well, well - her sons send a parcel through my hands every season, and never once has a reply gone back. I will tie it myself, double knot, and it goes on the next boat. Take this for your trouble, and tell her it is safe with me.
Have you given it to Tang Cuiping yet? She is at Hive Ridge Landing, north along the trade road. Please hurry - before I lose my courage and ask for it back.
Your pack is full - there is no room even for a letter. Make some space and come back.

quests.title: Offerings for the Mist
dialog: Every day the offerings must reach the shrine: meat for the table of the gods, and hair from the tails of the Forest Tormentors, woven into prayer cords. Whatever the shrine does not need feeds the village and keeps us warm. As long as the offerings reach the shrine, the mist keeps us hidden. The gods ask little - but they ask every day.

quests.title: Tell me about the white mist.
dialog: It is not weather. Weather comes and goes - the mist stays inside our fences and nowhere else. It came down the night Hu Lan and his horde burned the woods, and their fire walked right past us. We believe it is a gift of the gods who guard this village, and a gift must be answered. An offering at the shrine, every day. The day the offerings stop, the mist will lift - and I do not wish to see what waits outside when it does.

quests.title: Do you remember me?
dialog: The mist knows you now. When you walk in, it parts a little wider - I have seen it. The gods remember those who fed their table.

quests.title: Offerings for the Mist
quests.mission: Collect 100 portions of Dreadmaw Meat; Collect 200 locks of Tormentor Tail Hair
dialog: Every day the offerings must reach the shrine: meat for the table of the gods, and hair from the tails of the Forest Tormentors, woven into prayer cords. Today the bearers turned back - there were too many beasts on the path. I need new offerings: one hundred portions of Dreadmaw meat and two hundred locks of Tormentor tail hair. Whatever the shrine does not need will feed the village and keep us warm. The beasts give up what the gods accept only to one who carries this task, so the meat and the hair will fall to you only once you agree. Will you help us keep the mist?
May the mist guide you. Hunt the Dreadmaws and the Forest Tormentors around the village. Not every beast gives what the gods accept - about one Dreadmaw in four, one Tormentor in three.
Then rest a while. The mist will hold... for today.
Not yet enough. The gods ask one hundred portions of meat and two hundred locks of hair.
Your pack is too full for what I have for you. Make some room and come back.

The gods will be pleased, and the village will eat well tonight. I will carry the offerings to the shrine myself at dawn. Take this with our thanks. The bearers can manage the daily offerings again - you have given the mist enough strength for many seasons.
You have gathered all the offerings. Bring them to Yuanjue in the Forgotten Village.
You have carried our offerings three times already. The gods have seen your devotion - let the village do the rest now.

The offerings did not reach the shrine again today. The beasts grow bolder with every season. One hundred portions of Dreadmaw meat and two hundred locks of Tormentor tail hair, as before. Will you help us once more?

quests.title: Bones Under the Crosses
dialog: You see the crosses? The raiders came at night. They burned the houses, and those they caught they hung on the crosses at the edge of the fields - a warning to anyone who would rebuild. Nobody ever came to take them down. For years the Mystic Poison Tigers denned among the crosses and dug at the bones. Now the fields are quiet at night, and my people can finally rest.

quests.title: Arrows in the Bark
dialog: On the night of the fire I was waiting for someone. A hunter from Nanzhang - he crossed the Ashen Fields whenever the moon was full. He promised he would come that night. For so long I thought he simply stayed away. Then his arrows were found in the bark of the old trees that walk the fields - white-fletched, with goose feathers. He was fighting his way to me. He did not forget.

quests.title: Come Home
dialog: He always talked about his grandmother. Granny Hua, in Nanzhang, by the old cemetery. She kept the geese for his feathers, and she kept his dinner warm however late he came home. She has his arrows now. She knows he did not just walk away. I think she still sets out a bowl for him - and I think, somewhere, he has finally come home to eat it.

quests.title: What happened to your village?
dialog: It was a farming village - barley, millet, a few goats. We had no walls and nothing worth stealing, so we thought nobody would ever come. They came at night. Riders with torches. They burned the houses with the people inside, and those who ran they caught and hung on the crosses at the edge of the fields - so that nobody would ever settle here again. Nobody did. Only the tigers, and me.

quests.title: Who are you waiting for?
dialog: A hunter from Nanzhang. He used to cross the Ashen Fields whenever the moon was full, with a hare over his shoulder and some silly story about how he caught it. That night he promised he would come. I stood by the well and watched the fields, and then the fire came. I am still standing by the well. I know it is foolish - but what else should a ghost do, if not wait?

quests.title: Do you remember me?
dialog: He tried to reach me that night... I know it now. I am not waiting anymore - but I will stay a little longer, to watch over the others.

quests.title: Come Home
quests.mission: Bring the arrows to Granny Hua in Nanzhang
dialog: He always talked about his grandmother. Granny Hua, in Nanzhang, by the old cemetery. She kept the geese for his feathers, and she kept his dinner warm however late he came home. If she is still alive, she is still waiting for him. Just like I was. I cannot leave this place. Will you take his arrows to her? Then she will know he did not just walk away... and both of us can stop waiting.
I have tied them together with a strip of my sleeve. Granny Hua lives by the cemetery in Nanzhang. Be gentle with her.
Then I will keep them here a while longer. Arrows do not mind waiting.
Granny Hua lives by the cemetery in Nanzhang. Please - she has waited long enough.

White goose feathers... I plucked these myself. These are his. So he never came home because he could not. All these years I thought he had grown tired of an old woman's cooking. Thank you, traveler. Take this for your kindness - and tonight I will set out two bowls: one for him, and one for whoever he was walking to that night.
Have you found Granny Hua yet? She lives by the cemetery in Nanzhang. Give her the arrows - she will know them.
Your pack is too full to carry his arrows. Make some room and come back.

quests.title: Bones Under the Crosses
quests.mission: Hunt 300 Mystic Poison Tigers; Slay 1 Mystic Poison Tiger Champion
dialog: You see the crosses? The raiders came at night. They burned the houses, and those they caught they hung on the crosses at the edge of the fields - a warning to anyone who would rebuild. Nobody ever came to take them down. Now the Mystic Poison Tigers den among the crosses and dig at the bones. Every night I hear them scratching. I cannot go on while my people cannot rest. Drive the tigers from the crosses - three hundred of them, and the great one that leads them.
Thank you... The tigers den all around the ruins and the crosses. The one that leads them is a Champion - bigger than the rest, slow to anger and much slower to die.
Then go in peace. I have waited a long time - I can wait a little longer.
I still hear them scratching at night. Three hundred tigers, and the great one - then the dead can sleep.
Your pack is too full for what I have for you. Make some room and come back.

Listen... no scratching. For the first time since the fire, the fields are quiet. I could not bury them, and I could not leave them. You did the one thing I could not do. Take this - it belonged to the village, and the village has no use for it anymore.
The tigers are driven from the crosses. Return to Yue Ying at the well in the Ashen Ruins.

quests.title: Arrows in the Bark
dialog: On the night of the fire I was waiting for someone. A hunter from Nanzhang - he crossed the Ashen Fields whenever the moon was full. He promised he would come that night. He never did. I thought he simply stayed away. But the old trees that walk the fields have arrows in their bark - white-fletched, like his. He was the only hunter in Nanzhang who used white goose feathers. He was fighting his way to me. Bring me thirty of his arrows. Only someone who is looking will find them - they will come to you once you agree.
The Elder Yeoha and the Ancient Yeoha wander the fields not far from the ruins. Look closely at their bark - about one in five still holds one of his arrows.
I understand. It is only a ghost's question... I have asked it of the wind for years.
Thirty arrows... I want to hold every one of them. Please - the trees are still out there.
Your pack is too full for what I have for you. Make some room and come back.

These are his. I can still see where he trimmed the feathers, the way he always did. He did not forget me. He fought the trees all night to reach me - and all this time I thought he had stayed away. Take this... you gave me back the one thing the fire did not take.
You have found his arrows. Return to Yue Ying at the well in the Ashen Ruins.
